Just as this tree is not perfected except by good fruit, faith is not perfected except by refraining from what God has forbidden" [[Hadith no. 161; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]].

The wisdom in its likening faith to the palm among all other trees is that, since it is the most similar of trees to a human being, it was likened to him. For every tree, when its top is cut off, branches out from its sides, but the palm, when its top is cut off, dries up and its root perishes. Also, it resembles a human being and other animals in pollination, since it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best wealth is a pollinated palm-row and a well-tended mount" [[Hadith no. 162; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/270.]].

Among this is the hadith of Ibn Umar: the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "There is a tree among trees whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is." People began to name the trees of the desert, but it came to my mind that it was the palm, then I looked and I was the youngest of the people, so I was too shy and kept silent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm" [[Hadith no. 163.]]. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "O my son, if you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than such-and-such," because it is from the tree of Adam [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 1/481, no. 12460.]].

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Honor your aunt." It was said: "And who is our aunt, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The palm" [[Hadith no. 164; Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/338, no. 35300; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]]. This is because when God created Adam, a portion of his clay was set aside, and from it He created the palm. God said: ﴿God strikes the likenesses for people, that they may remember﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 25.]]. ﴿And the likeness of a corrupt word﴾, which is shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿is like a corrupt tree﴾, which is the colocynth.

Ibn Abbas said: this is a likeness that God struck, and He did not create this tree on the face of the earth.

﴿Uprooted﴾: pulled up. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "loosened." Al-Dahhak said: "cut off from the roots." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "it is taken wherever it is, with certainty." ﴿From above the earth; it has no stability.﴾ Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word ascends from him, nor righteous deed.

﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾: God confirms their faith and their deeds through the word and the making firm, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ Meaning in the grave; and it has been said: "in the life of this world" means in the grave, in the sight of God, the Exalted, and "in the Hereafter" means when they are resurrected.

Muqatil said: this is because when the believer dies, God sends to him an angel called Ruman, who enters his grave and says to him: "There will come to you now two black angels who will ask you: Who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, and who are your leaders? Answer them with what you were upon in your life." Then he (Ruman) leaves, and the two angels enter, Munkar and Nakir, black and blue, harsh and coarse, their eyes like flashing lightning and their voices like a violent wind, with maces. They sit him up and question him, and they do not notice the entry of Ruman. He says: "My Lord is God, my Prophet is Muhammad, and my religion is Islam." They say to him: "Blessed by God," then they say: "O God, please him as You pleased Yourself." A door of Paradise is opened for him in his grave, from which gifts come to him. When they leave him, he is told: "Sleep the sleep of the bride." This is the making firm. ﴿And God leads the wrongdoers astray﴾, meaning He curses them. When the disbeliever is visited by the two angels, they say to him: "Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not know and you were not guided; you lived in rebellion and died in wretchedness." Then they say to him: "Sleep the sleep of one who is struck," and a door of Hell is opened for him from his grave, and they strike him with that mace, and he shrieks a shriek that every creature hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), and every one who hears his voice curses him. This is His saying ﴿and those who curse will curse them﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 159.]].

Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the believer's soul, and said: "His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' They rebuke him and say a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' This is the last of the angels' questions, and God makes him firm, so he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out in the sky: 'Make My servant firm.'" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281; Musnad Ahmad: 4/287, with slight variation.]] Then the saying of God was revealed: ﴿God makes firm those who believe﴾, the verse.

Ibn Abbas said concerning this verse: when death attends the believer, the angels witness it, greet him with peace, and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he sits up in his grave, and he is asked: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is God." He is asked: "Who is your messenger?" He says: "Muhammad." He is asked: "What is your testimony?" He says: "I testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then his grave is widened as far as his eye can see. This is His saying ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Abu Nadrah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his beloved ones disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mallet in his hand and seats him up and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he is a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The angel says to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wants to rise toward it, but he is told: 'Be still.' Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, you did not recite, and you were not guided.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel strikes him with the mallet, a blow that every creature of God hears except the two weighty ones."

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is none among us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer (mitraq) without being terrified by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah makes firm those who believe" [verse 27]. [166] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/637, no. 42509; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281.]]

Abu Hurayrah said: "The deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer would be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the good deeds—charity, kinship ties and kindness—would be at his feet. People would pray over him, and then he would be approached from the direction of his head, and it would say, 'Prayer, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his right, and it would say, 'Zakat, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his left, and it would say, 'Fasting, come forward,' and it would enter. Then his voice would come from the direction of his feet, and it would say, 'Good deeds, come forward,' and it would enter. He would be told, 'Sit up,' and he would sit up, the sun having been depicted to him and the time of sunset having arrived. He would be told, 'Tell us what we ask you.' He would say, 'Leave me until I pray.' It would be said, 'You will indeed do so. Tell us what we ask you about.' He would say, 'What do you want to ask me?' They would say, 'What do you think of this man who was among you, and what did he testify to?' He would say, 'Muhammad?' They would say, 'Yes.' He would say, 'I testify that he is truly the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him.' It would be said to him, 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then his grave would be widened for him to seventy cubits and it would be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has prepared for you therein,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has averted from you had you disobeyed Him,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then his soul would be placed in a pleasant breeze, and it is a green bird hanging from the trees of Paradise, and his body would be returned to the dust from which it was created. This is the meaning of His saying: 'Allah makes firm those who believe' [verse 27] up to His saying, 'and in the Hereafter' [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/283.]]."

And on the authority of Abu Nafi' who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking by a pool of water, and I was walking behind him, he (ﷺ) said: 'May you not be guided, may you not be guided,' three times." [167] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/325.]]

Abu Nafi' said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with me?' He said: 'I did not mean you; I mean the owner of this grave. He will be asked about me, and he will claim that he does not know me.' It was a grave that had been sprinkled with water when its occupant was buried."

Abu al-Qasim al-Sulami informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Khayyat, who said: I heard Suhayl ibn Jabir al-'Ataki say: "I saw Yazid ibn 'Uthman in a dream after his death, and I asked him, 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Two angels came to me in my grave, harsh and coarse, and said, "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" I seized my white beard and said to them, "Is this how someone like me is addressed, when I have known the people's answer to your question for eighty years?" They left and said, "Did you write down from Jarir ibn 'Uthman?" I said, "Yes." They said, "He used to hate 'Ali, so Allah hated him."' " [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/363.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 18–27 (part 1 of 2):

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 18.]]. The grammarians differed over the nominative case of *mathal* (likeness). Al-Farra' said: the likeness is attributed to those who disbelieve, while the likeness itself belongs to the deeds, because the Arabs put the nouns first since they are more definite, and then bring the predicate that is stated about them together with their referent. The meaning of the verse is: the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is like ashes. Compare His saying ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 7.]], meaning: He perfected the creation of everything. And His saying ﴿On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 60.]], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied against God blackened, evilly blackened. In the verse there is an implied element, whose meaning is: and the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is not to be recited to you. Then it begins, and he proceeds to explain it, saying: "their deeds are like ashes."

If you wish, you may make *mathal* an attribute and say: "Those who disbelieve in their Lord—their deeds are like ashes ﴿which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾." The day is described as stormy, though stormy is a property of the wind, because the wind occurs on it, just as one says "a cold day" or "a hot day," since cold and heat occur in it; and "a sleeping night" and "a fasting day." God said ﴿and the day as one that makes things visible﴾ [[Surah Yunus: 67.]], and the night and the day indicate this. The poet said:

*Two cloudy days and one sunny day*

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

Al-Farra' also said: if you wish, you may say "on a day of stormy wind" (*fi yawm ʿasūf*), and if you wish, you may say "on a day of wind that is stormy" (*fi yawm ʿāṣif al-rīḥ*), omitting "the wind" because it has been mentioned before. This is like the poet's saying:

*When a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed*

[[Lisan al-Arab: 9/248; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

meaning: the sun is eclipsed (*kasif al-shams*).

It has also been said that it is an attribute of the wind, but since it came after "day," its i'rab (grammatical case inflection) follows it, as is said in "a hole of a lizard, ruined" and similar expressions. This is a likeness that God struck for the deeds of the disbeliever, meaning: they gain nothing from their deeds that they performed in the world, because they associated partners with God in them, just as the ashes that the wind scatters are of no benefit. This is His saying ﴿they have no power over anything they have earned﴾, meaning the disbelievers, from what they earned in the world, over anything in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the far-off error.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth﴾.

The people of Kufa, except Amir, read *khāliq al-samāwāti wal-arḍ* (Creator of the heavens and the earth), as an emphatic form (of the active participle, on the pattern of *fāʿil*). See al-Tabari's commentary: 13/260.

The others read *khalaqa al-samāwāti* (He created the heavens), in the sense of ﴿with truth﴾. The exegetes said: He did not create them in vain, but He created them for a great purpose.

﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation﴾: He will replace you with what is better, more excellent, and more obedient than you. ﴿That is not difficult for God﴾: it is not unattainable or impossible for Him. ﴿And they will all appear before God﴾: they will come out of their graves and be made manifest before God, all of them. The verb is in the future. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾: meaning the followers say to the leaders who were followed: ﴿We were your followers﴾. *Tabaʿ* is the plural of *tābiʿ* (follower), like *ḥāris* and *ḥaras* (guard, guards). It has also been said: *rāṣid* and *rasad* (watcher, watchers), and *nāfir* and *nafr* (one who flees, those who flee). It is also permissible for *tabaʿ* to be a verbal noun that was used as a name, meaning "we were people of following." See al-Qurtubi's commentary: 9/355.

﴿Can you then relieve us of anything from the punishment of God?﴾, meaning: can you, together with your ... , ward off God's punishment from us? The leaders say: ﴿If God had guided us, we would have guided you﴾, up to His saying ﴿no place of escape﴾: no refuge and no escape. It may be both a verbal noun and a noun. It is said: *ḥāṣa fulān ʿan kadhā*, meaning he fled and turned away from it, *yaḥīṣu ḥaysan* and *ḥiyūṣan* and *ḥiyṣānan*.

Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire, "Come, let us lament," and they will lament for five hundred years, and the lamenting will not benefit them. They will say, "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for five hundred years, and the patience will not benefit them. Then they will say: ﴿It is the same for us whether we lament or are patient; we have no place of escape.﴾

﴿And the Satan will say﴾, meaning Iblis, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning when the matter has been finished: the people of Paradise have been admitted to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

Muqatil said: a pulpit of fire will be placed for him, and he will climb it, and the disbelievers will gather around him with their leaders. ﴿God promised you the promise of truth﴾, which will be fulfilled for you. ﴿And I promised you, and I broke it. I had no authority over you﴾, meaning no dominion, no kingdom, no proof, and no insight. ﴿Except that I called you﴾: this is an exception of a disconnected kind (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*), whose meaning is: except for those who called you. ﴿So you responded to me. Do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ for responding to me and following me without authority and without proof. ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾: I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper, I will not give you relief nor you me.

The common readers read *bi-muṣrikhiyya* with a fatha on the *yāʾ*. Al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read it with a kasra on the *yāʾ*. The original form is *bi-muṣrikhiyyīn*: the *nūn* was dropped because of the possessive construction, and the *yāʾ* of the plural was assimilated into the *yāʾ* of the first person possessive. Whoever reads with a fatha does so because of the doubling, and whoever reads with a kasra does so because two unvocalized letters came together, so it was vocalized with a kasra, since the *yāʾ* is a sister of the kasra. See al-Qurtubi: 9/357.

﴿I disbelieve in your having associated me with God before﴾: that is, it is not possible for me to be a partner to God in what you associated me with through your obedience to me. I mock that. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers, the disbelievers who place obedience to creatures where it does not belong, will have a painful punishment.﴾

Utbah ibn Amir narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith about intercession, that he said: "Jesus (peace be upon him) will say: 'Go to that unlettered Prophet, and they will come to me, and God will permit me to rise, and my assembly will be stirred up with the most fragrant scent anyone has smelled, until I come and he intercedes for me, and places for me a light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot.'"

Then the disbelievers will say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them; so who will intercede for us?" They will say: "There is no one but Iblis, he is the one who led us astray." They will come and say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so get up and intercede for us, for you led us astray." He will say: he rises from his assembly, and a stench rises from it that is the most foul anyone has smelled. Then their wailing will grow intense, and at that moment he will say: ﴿God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke it﴾ [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/327; Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/263.]].

...﴿And those who believed will be admitted﴾, up to His saying ﴿therein is peace﴾: God will greet them with peace, and the angels will greet them with peace.

﴿Do you not see, O Muhammad?﴾, meaning: God knows, through my informing you, ﴿how God struck a likeness: a good word﴾, meaning God has clarified its likeness: a good word, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿like a good tree﴾, which is the date palm. This is shown by the hadith of Utayb al-Hijab, who said: Abu al-Aliyah was my guardian (*amīn*). One day he came to me at my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I went with him to Anas ibn Malik. I entered upon him, and a tray with fresh dates was brought.

Anas said: "Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree that God mentioned in His Book: ﴿Do you not see how God struck a likeness: a good word, like a good tree﴾." Then Anas said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was brought a basket of unripe dates, and he recited this verse."

The meaning of the verse is: like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of the fruit is omitted because the food indicates it.

Abu Dhabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: "This is a tree in Paradise, ﴿whose root is firm in the earth, and whose branches are high in the sky﴾. Likewise, the root of this word is established in the heart of the believer through knowledge, affirmation, and sincerity. When he speaks the testimony, it ascends to the sky, and it is not recorded until it reaches God, the Exalted. God said: ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and righteous deeds raise it﴾ [[Surah Fatir: 10.]]."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has a pillar of light whose base is beneath the seventh earth and whose top is beneath the Throne. When the servant says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' that pillar trembles, and God, mighty and majestic, says: 'Be still!' It says: 'How can I be still, when You have not forgiven the one who said it?' The Lord says: 'I have forgiven him,' and then it is still."

The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "Increase your shaking of that pillar" [[Al-Mawdu'at of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/167; Majma' al-Zawa'id, abridged: 10/82.]].

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾, meaning it gives its fruit. The commentators differed about *ḥīn* (season).

Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zayd said: every year.

Ikrimah said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "I vowed to cut off a man's hand from such-and-such a year and season; what is your opinion about it?" Ibn Abbas said: I said to him: "Do not cut off his hand; imprison him for a year" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/274.]].

Indeed Ibn Abbas says: *ḥīn* has two kinds: a season that is known and changes, and a season that is not known. As for the unknown season: ﴿and you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [[Surah Sad: 88.]]. As for the known one: ﴿it gives its fruit every season﴾, which is the period from one year to the next.

Umar said: "You are right, O client of Ibn Abbas, and you have done well" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Nahhas, abridged: 3/528.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and al-Hasan said: every six months, from its *ʿarām* (the first blossoming, the sprouting of the spathe) to its bearing.

Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about a man who swore not to speak to his brother for a *ḥīn*. He said: "The *ḥīn* is seven months," and he recited this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The *ḥīn* is two months, because the palm does not have its fruit except for two months."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿every season﴾ means every morning and evening; likewise the deed of the believer rises at the beginning of the day and at its end. This is also the narration of Abu Dhabyan from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Dahhak said: every hour, by night and by day, in winter and in summer; it is eaten at all times. Likewise the believer is never without good at all times.

Abu al-Hakam recited the likeness of faith to the tree: a tree is not a tree except through three things: a firm trunk, a standing root, and high branches. Likewise faith is not complete and does not stand except through three things: affirmation by the heart, speech by the tongue, and action by the body.

This is supported by what Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Faith is affirmation by the heart, acknowledgment by the tongue, and action by the limbs" [[Hadith no. 160.]].

Humayd al-Tawil narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the likeness of this religion is that of a firm tree: faith is its root, zakat is its branch, fasting is its roots, calling to God is its shoots, good character is its leaves, and refraining from what God has forbidden is its greenness. Just as this tree is not perfected except by good fruit, faith is not perfected except by refraining from what God has forbidden" [[Hadith no. 161; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]].

The wisdom in its likening faith to the palm among all other trees is that, since it is the most similar of trees to a human being, it was likened to him. For every tree, when its top is cut off, branches out from its sides, but the palm, when its top is cut off, dries up and its root perishes. Also, it resembles a human being and other animals in pollination, since it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best wealth is a pollinated palm-row and a well-tended mount" [[Hadith no. 162; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/270.]].

Among this is the hadith of Ibn Umar: the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "There is a tree among trees whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is." People began to name the trees of the desert, but it came to my mind that it was the palm, then I looked and I was the youngest of the people, so I was too shy and kept silent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm" [[Hadith no. 163.]]. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "O my son, if you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than such-and-such," because it is from the tree of Adam [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 1/481, no. 12460.]].

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Honor your aunt." It was said: "And who is our aunt, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The palm" [[Hadith no. 164; Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/338, no. 35300; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]]. This is because when God created Adam, a portion of his clay was set aside, and from it He created the palm. God said: ﴿God strikes the likenesses for people, that they may remember﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 25.]]. ﴿And the likeness of a corrupt word﴾, which is shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿is like a corrupt tree﴾, which is the colocynth.

Ibn Abbas said: this is a likeness that God struck, and He did not create this tree on the face of the earth.

﴿Uprooted﴾: pulled up. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "loosened." Al-Dahhak said: "cut off from the roots." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "it is taken wherever it is, with certainty." ﴿From above the earth; it has no stability.﴾ Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word ascends from him, nor righteous deed.

﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾: God confirms their faith and their deeds through the word and the making firm, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ Meaning in the grave; and it has been said: "in the life of this world" means in the grave, in the sight of God, the Exalted, and "in the Hereafter" means when they are resurrected.

Muqatil said: this is because when the believer dies, God sends to him an angel called Ruman, who enters his grave and says to him: "There will come to you now two black angels who will ask you: Who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, and who are your leaders? Answer them with what you were upon in your life." Then he (Ruman) leaves, and the two angels enter, Munkar and Nakir, black and blue, harsh and coarse, their eyes like flashing lightning and their voices like a violent wind, with maces. They sit him up and question him, and they do not notice the entry of Ruman. He says: "My Lord is God, my Prophet is Muhammad, and my religion is Islam." They say to him: "Blessed by God," then they say: "O God, please him as You pleased Yourself." A door of Paradise is opened for him in his grave, from which gifts come to him. When they leave him, he is told: "Sleep the sleep of the bride." This is the making firm. ﴿And God leads the wrongdoers astray﴾, meaning He curses them. When the disbeliever is visited by the two angels, they say to him: "Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not know and you were not guided; you lived in rebellion and died in wretchedness." Then they say to him: "Sleep the sleep of one who is struck," and a door of Hell is opened for him from his grave, and they strike him with that mace, and he shrieks a shriek that every creature hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), and every one who hears his voice curses him. This is His saying ﴿and those who curse will curse them﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 159.]].

Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the believer's soul, and said: "His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' They rebuke him and say a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' This is the last of the angels' questions, and God makes him firm, so he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out in the sky: 'Make My servant firm.'" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281; Musnad Ahmad: 4/287, with slight variation.]] Then the saying of God was revealed: ﴿God makes firm those who believe﴾, the verse.

Ibn Abbas said concerning this verse: when death attends the believer, the angels witness it, greet him with peace, and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he sits up in his grave, and he is asked: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is God." He is asked: "Who is your messenger?" He says: "Muhammad." He is asked: "What is your testimony?" He says: "I testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then his grave is widened as far as his eye can see. This is His saying ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Abu Nadrah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his beloved ones disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mallet in his hand and seats him up and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he is a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The angel says to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wants to rise toward it, but he is told: 'Be still.' Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, you did not recite, and you were not guided.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel strikes him with the mallet, a blow that every creature of God hears except the two weighty ones."

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is none among us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer (mitraq) without being terrified by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah makes firm those who believe" [verse 27]. [166] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/637, no. 42509; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281.]]

Abu Hurayrah said: "The deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer would be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the good deeds—charity, kinship ties and kindness—would be at his feet. People would pray over him, and then he would be approached from the direction of his head, and it would say, 'Prayer, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his right, and it would say, 'Zakat, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his left, and it would say, 'Fasting, come forward,' and it would enter. Then his voice would come from the direction of his feet, and it would say, 'Good deeds, come forward,' and it would enter. He would be told, 'Sit up,' and he would sit up, the sun having been depicted to him and the time of sunset having arrived. He would be told, 'Tell us what we ask you.' He would say, 'Leave me until I pray.' It would be said, 'You will indeed do so. Tell us what we ask you about.' He would say, 'What do you want to ask me?' They would say, 'What do you think of this man who was among you, and what did he testify to?' He would say, 'Muhammad?' They would say, 'Yes.' He would say, 'I testify that he is truly the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him.' It would be said to him, 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then his grave would be widened for him to seventy cubits and it would be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has prepared for you therein,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has averted from you had you disobeyed Him,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then his soul would be placed in a pleasant breeze, and it is a green bird hanging from the trees of Paradise, and his body would be returned to the dust from which it was created. This is the meaning of His saying: 'Allah makes firm those who believe' [verse 27] up to His saying, 'and in the Hereafter' [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/283.]]."

And on the authority of Abu Nafi' who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking by a pool of water, and I was walking behind him, he (ﷺ) said: 'May you not be guided, may you not be guided,' three times." [167] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/325.]]

Abu Nafi' said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with me?' He said: 'I did not mean you; I mean the owner of this grave. He will be asked about me, and he will claim that he does not know me.' It was a grave that had been sprinkled with water when its occupant was buried."

Abu al-Qasim al-Sulami informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Khayyat, who said: I heard Suhayl ibn Jabir al-'Ataki say: "I saw Yazid ibn 'Uthman in a dream after his death, and I asked him, 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Two angels came to me in my grave, harsh and coarse, and said, "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" I seized my white beard and said to them, "Is this how someone like me is addressed, when I have known the people's answer to your question for eighty years?" They left and said, "Did you write down from Jarir ibn 'Uthman?" I said, "Yes." They said, "He used to hate 'Ali, so Allah hated him."' " [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/363.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 18–27 (part 1 of 2):

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 18.]]. The grammarians differed over the nominative case of *mathal* (likeness). Al-Farra' said: the likeness is attributed to those who disbelieve, while the likeness itself belongs to the deeds, because the Arabs put the nouns first since they are more definite, and then bring the predicate that is stated about them together with their referent. The meaning of the verse is: the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is like ashes. Compare His saying ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 7.]], meaning: He perfected the creation of everything. And His saying ﴿On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 60.]], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied against God blackened, evilly blackened. In the verse there is an implied element, whose meaning is: and the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is not to be recited to you. Then it begins, and he proceeds to explain it, saying: "their deeds are like ashes."

If you wish, you may make *mathal* an attribute and say: "Those who disbelieve in their Lord—their deeds are like ashes ﴿which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾." The day is described as stormy, though stormy is a property of the wind, because the wind occurs on it, just as one says "a cold day" or "a hot day," since cold and heat occur in it; and "a sleeping night" and "a fasting day." God said ﴿and the day as one that makes things visible﴾ [[Surah Yunus: 67.]], and the night and the day indicate this. The poet said:

*Two cloudy days and one sunny day*

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

Al-Farra' also said: if you wish, you may say "on a day of stormy wind" (*fi yawm ʿasūf*), and if you wish, you may say "on a day of wind that is stormy" (*fi yawm ʿāṣif al-rīḥ*), omitting "the wind" because it has been mentioned before. This is like the poet's saying:

*When a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed*

[[Lisan al-Arab: 9/248; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

meaning: the sun is eclipsed (*kasif al-shams*).

It has also been said that it is an attribute of the wind, but since it came after "day," its i'rab (grammatical case inflection) follows it, as is said in "a hole of a lizard, ruined" and similar expressions. This is a likeness that God struck for the deeds of the disbeliever, meaning: they gain nothing from their deeds that they performed in the world, because they associated partners with God in them, just as the ashes that the wind scatters are of no benefit. This is His saying ﴿they have no power over anything they have earned﴾, meaning the disbelievers, from what they earned in the world, over anything in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the far-off error.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth﴾.

The people of Kufa, except Amir, read *khāliq al-samāwāti wal-arḍ* (Creator of the heavens and the earth), as an emphatic form (of the active participle, on the pattern of *fāʿil*). See al-Tabari's commentary: 13/260.

The others read *khalaqa al-samāwāti* (He created the heavens), in the sense of ﴿with truth﴾. The exegetes said: He did not create them in vain, but He created them for a great purpose.

﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation﴾: He will replace you with what is better, more excellent, and more obedient than you. ﴿That is not difficult for God﴾: it is not unattainable or impossible for Him. ﴿And they will all appear before God﴾: they will come out of their graves and be made manifest before God, all of them. The verb is in the future. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾: meaning the followers say to the leaders who were followed: ﴿We were your followers﴾. *Tabaʿ* is the plural of *tābiʿ* (follower), like *ḥāris* and *ḥaras* (guard, guards). It has also been said: *rāṣid* and *rasad* (watcher, watchers), and *nāfir* and *nafr* (one who flees, those who flee). It is also permissible for *tabaʿ* to be a verbal noun that was used as a name, meaning "we were people of following." See al-Qurtubi's commentary: 9/355.

﴿Can you then relieve us of anything from the punishment of God?﴾, meaning: can you, together with your ... , ward off God's punishment from us? The leaders say: ﴿If God had guided us, we would have guided you﴾, up to His saying ﴿no place of escape﴾: no refuge and no escape. It may be both a verbal noun and a noun. It is said: *ḥāṣa fulān ʿan kadhā*, meaning he fled and turned away from it, *yaḥīṣu ḥaysan* and *ḥiyūṣan* and *ḥiyṣānan*.

Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire, "Come, let us lament," and they will lament for five hundred years, and the lamenting will not benefit them. They will say, "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for five hundred years, and the patience will not benefit them. Then they will say: ﴿It is the same for us whether we lament or are patient; we have no place of escape.﴾

﴿And the Satan will say﴾, meaning Iblis, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning when the matter has been finished: the people of Paradise have been admitted to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

Muqatil said: a pulpit of fire will be placed for him, and he will climb it, and the disbelievers will gather around him with their leaders. ﴿God promised you the promise of truth﴾, which will be fulfilled for you. ﴿And I promised you, and I broke it. I had no authority over you﴾, meaning no dominion, no kingdom, no proof, and no insight. ﴿Except that I called you﴾: this is an exception of a disconnected kind (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*), whose meaning is: except for those who called you. ﴿So you responded to me. Do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ for responding to me and following me without authority and without proof. ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾: I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper, I will not give you relief nor you me.

The common readers read *bi-muṣrikhiyya* with a fatha on the *yāʾ*. Al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read it with a kasra on the *yāʾ*. The original form is *bi-muṣrikhiyyīn*: the *nūn* was dropped because of the possessive construction, and the *yāʾ* of the plural was assimilated into the *yāʾ* of the first person possessive. Whoever reads with a fatha does so because of the doubling, and whoever reads with a kasra does so because two unvocalized letters came together, so it was vocalized with a kasra, since the *yāʾ* is a sister of the kasra. See al-Qurtubi: 9/357.

﴿I disbelieve in your having associated me with God before﴾: that is, it is not possible for me to be a partner to God in what you associated me with through your obedience to me. I mock that. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers, the disbelievers who place obedience to creatures where it does not belong, will have a painful punishment.﴾

Utbah ibn Amir narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith about intercession, that he said: "Jesus (peace be upon him) will say: 'Go to that unlettered Prophet, and they will come to me, and God will permit me to rise, and my assembly will be stirred up with the most fragrant scent anyone has smelled, until I come and he intercedes for me, and places for me a light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot.'"

Then the disbelievers will say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them; so who will intercede for us?" They will say: "There is no one but Iblis, he is the one who led us astray." They will come and say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so get up and intercede for us, for you led us astray." He will say: he rises from his assembly, and a stench rises from it that is the most foul anyone has smelled. Then their wailing will grow intense, and at that moment he will say: ﴿God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke it﴾ [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/327; Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/263.]].

...﴿And those who believed will be admitted﴾, up to His saying ﴿therein is peace﴾: God will greet them with peace, and the angels will greet them with peace.

﴿Do you not see, O Muhammad?﴾, meaning: God knows, through my informing you, ﴿how God struck a likeness: a good word﴾, meaning God has clarified its likeness: a good word, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿like a good tree﴾, which is the date palm. This is shown by the hadith of Utayb al-Hijab, who said: Abu al-Aliyah was my guardian (*amīn*). One day he came to me at my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I went with him to Anas ibn Malik. I entered upon him, and a tray with fresh dates was brought.

Anas said: "Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree that God mentioned in His Book: ﴿Do you not see how God struck a likeness: a good word, like a good tree﴾." Then Anas said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was brought a basket of unripe dates, and he recited this verse."

The meaning of the verse is: like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of the fruit is omitted because the food indicates it.

Abu Dhabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: "This is a tree in Paradise, ﴿whose root is firm in the earth, and whose branches are high in the sky﴾. Likewise, the root of this word is established in the heart of the believer through knowledge, affirmation, and sincerity. When he speaks the testimony, it ascends to the sky, and it is not recorded until it reaches God, the Exalted. God said: ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and righteous deeds raise it﴾ [[Surah Fatir: 10.]]."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has a pillar of light whose base is beneath the seventh earth and whose top is beneath the Throne. When the servant says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' that pillar trembles, and God, mighty and majestic, says: 'Be still!' It says: 'How can I be still, when You have not forgiven the one who said it?' The Lord says: 'I have forgiven him,' and then it is still."

The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "Increase your shaking of that pillar" [[Al-Mawdu'at of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/167; Majma' al-Zawa'id, abridged: 10/82.]].

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾, meaning it gives its fruit. The commentators differed about *ḥīn* (season).

Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zayd said: every year.

Ikrimah said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "I vowed to cut off a man's hand from such-and-such a year and season; what is your opinion about it?" Ibn Abbas said: I said to him: "Do not cut off his hand; imprison him for a year" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/274.]].

Indeed Ibn Abbas says: *ḥīn* has two kinds: a season that is known and changes, and a season that is not known. As for the unknown season: ﴿and you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [[Surah Sad: 88.]]. As for the known one: ﴿it gives its fruit every season﴾, which is the period from one year to the next.

Umar said: "You are right, O client of Ibn Abbas, and you have done well" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Nahhas, abridged: 3/528.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and al-Hasan said: every six months, from its *ʿarām* (the first blossoming, the sprouting of the spathe) to its bearing.

Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about a man who swore not to speak to his brother for a *ḥīn*. He said: "The *ḥīn* is seven months," and he recited this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The *ḥīn* is two months, because the palm does not have its fruit except for two months."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿every season﴾ means every morning and evening; likewise the deed of the believer rises at the beginning of the day and at its end. This is also the narration of Abu Dhabyan from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Dahhak said: every hour, by night and by day, in winter and in summer; it is eaten at all times. Likewise the believer is never without good at all times.

Abu al-Hakam recited the likeness of faith to the tree: a tree is not a tree except through three things: a firm trunk, a standing root, and high branches. Likewise faith is not complete and does not stand except through three things: affirmation by the heart, speech by the tongue, and action by the body.

This is supported by what Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Faith is affirmation by the heart, acknowledgment by the tongue, and action by the limbs" [[Hadith no. 160.]].

Humayd al-Tawil narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the likeness of this religion is that of a firm tree: faith is its root, zakat is its branch, fasting is its roots, calling to God is its shoots, good character is its leaves, and refraining from what God has forbidden is its greenness. Just as this tree is not perfected except by good fruit, faith is not perfected except by refraining from what God has forbidden" [[Hadith no. 161; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]].

The wisdom in its likening faith to the palm among all other trees is that, since it is the most similar of trees to a human being, it was likened to him. For every tree, when its top is cut off, branches out from its sides, but the palm, when its top is cut off, dries up and its root perishes. Also, it resembles a human being and other animals in pollination, since it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best wealth is a pollinated palm-row and a well-tended mount" [[Hadith no. 162; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/270.]].

Among this is the hadith of Ibn Umar: the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "There is a tree among trees whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is." People began to name the trees of the desert, but it came to my mind that it was the palm, then I looked and I was the youngest of the people, so I was too shy and kept silent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm" [[Hadith no. 163.]]. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "O my son, if you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than such-and-such," because it is from the tree of Adam [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 1/481, no. 12460.]].

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Honor your aunt." It was said: "And who is our aunt, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The palm" [[Hadith no. 164; Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/338, no. 35300; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]]. This is because when God created Adam, a portion of his clay was set aside, and from it He created the palm. God said: ﴿God strikes the likenesses for people, that they may remember﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 25.]]. ﴿And the likeness of a corrupt word﴾, which is shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿is like a corrupt tree﴾, which is the colocynth.

Ibn Abbas said: this is a likeness that God struck, and He did not create this tree on the face of the earth.

﴿Uprooted﴾: pulled up. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "loosened." Al-Dahhak said: "cut off from the roots." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "it is taken wherever it is, with certainty." ﴿From above the earth; it has no stability.﴾ Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word ascends from him, nor righteous deed.

﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾: God confirms their faith and their deeds through the word and the making firm, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ Meaning in the grave; and it has been said: "in the life of this world" means in the grave, in the sight of God, the Exalted, and "in the Hereafter" means when they are resurrected.

Muqatil said: this is because when the believer dies, God sends to him an angel called Ruman, who enters his grave and says to him: "There will come to you now two black angels who will ask you: Who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, and who are your leaders? Answer them with what you were upon in your life." Then he (Ruman) leaves, and the two angels enter, Munkar and Nakir, black and blue, harsh and coarse, their eyes like flashing lightning and their voices like a violent wind, with maces. They sit him up and question him, and they do not notice the entry of Ruman. He says: "My Lord is God, my Prophet is Muhammad, and my religion is Islam." They say to him: "Blessed by God," then they say: "O God, please him as You pleased Yourself." A door of Paradise is opened for him in his grave, from which gifts come to him. When they leave him, he is told: "Sleep the sleep of the bride." This is the making firm. ﴿And God leads the wrongdoers astray﴾, meaning He curses them. When the disbeliever is visited by the two angels, they say to him: "Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not know and you were not guided; you lived in rebellion and died in wretchedness." Then they say to him: "Sleep the sleep of one who is struck," and a door of Hell is opened for him from his grave, and they strike him with that mace, and he shrieks a shriek that every creature hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), and every one who hears his voice curses him. This is His saying ﴿and those who curse will curse them﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 159.]].

Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the believer's soul, and said: "His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' They rebuke him and say a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' This is the last of the angels' questions, and God makes him firm, so he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out in the sky: 'Make My servant firm.'" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281; Musnad Ahmad: 4/287, with slight variation.]] Then the saying of God was revealed: ﴿God makes firm those who believe﴾, the verse.

Ibn Abbas said concerning this verse: when death attends the believer, the angels witness it, greet him with peace, and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he sits up in his grave, and he is asked: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is God." He is asked: "Who is your messenger?" He says: "Muhammad." He is asked: "What is your testimony?" He says: "I testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then his grave is widened as far as his eye can see. This is His saying ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Abu Nadrah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his beloved ones disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mallet in his hand and seats him up and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he is a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The angel says to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wants to rise toward it, but he is told: 'Be still.' Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, you did not recite, and you were not guided.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel strikes him with the mallet, a blow that every creature of God hears except the two weighty ones."

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is none among us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer (mitraq) without being terrified by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah makes firm those who believe" [verse 27]. [166] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/637, no. 42509; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281.]]

Abu Hurayrah said: "The deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer would be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the good deeds—charity, kinship ties and kindness—would be at his feet. People would pray over him, and then he would be approached from the direction of his head, and it would say, 'Prayer, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his right, and it would say, 'Zakat, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his left, and it would say, 'Fasting, come forward,' and it would enter. Then his voice would come from the direction of his feet, and it would say, 'Good deeds, come forward,' and it would enter. He would be told, 'Sit up,' and he would sit up, the sun having been depicted to him and the time of sunset having arrived. He would be told, 'Tell us what we ask you.' He would say, 'Leave me until I pray.' It would be said, 'You will indeed do so. Tell us what we ask you about.' He would say, 'What do you want to ask me?' They would say, 'What do you think of this man who was among you, and what did he testify to?' He would say, 'Muhammad?' They would say, 'Yes.' He would say, 'I testify that he is truly the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him.' It would be said to him, 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then his grave would be widened for him to seventy cubits and it would be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has prepared for you therein,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has averted from you had you disobeyed Him,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then his soul would be placed in a pleasant breeze, and it is a green bird hanging from the trees of Paradise, and his body would be returned to the dust from which it was created. This is the meaning of His saying: 'Allah makes firm those who believe' [verse 27] up to His saying, 'and in the Hereafter' [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/283.]]."

And on the authority of Abu Nafi' who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking by a pool of water, and I was walking behind him, he (ﷺ) said: 'May you not be guided, may you not be guided,' three times." [167] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/325.]]

Abu Nafi' said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with me?' He said: 'I did not mean you; I mean the owner of this grave. He will be asked about me, and he will claim that he does not know me.' It was a grave that had been sprinkled with water when its occupant was buried."

Abu al-Qasim al-Sulami informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Khayyat, who said: I heard Suhayl ibn Jabir al-'Ataki say: "I saw Yazid ibn 'Uthman in a dream after his death, and I asked him, 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Two angels came to me in my grave, harsh and coarse, and said, "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" I seized my white beard and said to them, "Is this how someone like me is addressed, when I have known the people's answer to your question for eighty years?" They left and said, "Did you write down from Jarir ibn 'Uthman?" I said, "Yes." They said, "He used to hate 'Ali, so Allah hated him."' " [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/363.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 18–27 (part 1 of 2):

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 18.]]. The grammarians differed over the nominative case of *mathal* (likeness). Al-Farra' said: the likeness is attributed to those who disbelieve, while the likeness itself belongs to the deeds, because the Arabs put the nouns first since they are more definite, and then bring the predicate that is stated about them together with their referent. The meaning of the verse is: the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is like ashes. Compare His saying ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 7.]], meaning: He perfected the creation of everything. And His saying ﴿On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 60.]], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied against God blackened, evilly blackened. In the verse there is an implied element, whose meaning is: and the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is not to be recited to you. Then it begins, and he proceeds to explain it, saying: "their deeds are like ashes."

If you wish, you may make *mathal* an attribute and say: "Those who disbelieve in their Lord—their deeds are like ashes ﴿which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾." The day is described as stormy, though stormy is a property of the wind, because the wind occurs on it, just as one says "a cold day" or "a hot day," since cold and heat occur in it; and "a sleeping night" and "a fasting day." God said ﴿and the day as one that makes things visible﴾ [[Surah Yunus: 67.]], and the night and the day indicate this. The poet said:

*Two cloudy days and one sunny day*

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

Al-Farra' also said: if you wish, you may say "on a day of stormy wind" (*fi yawm ʿasūf*), and if you wish, you may say "on a day of wind that is stormy" (*fi yawm ʿāṣif al-rīḥ*), omitting "the wind" because it has been mentioned before. This is like the poet's saying:

*When a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed*

[[Lisan al-Arab: 9/248; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

meaning: the sun is eclipsed (*kasif al-shams*).

It has also been said that it is an attribute of the wind, but since it came after "day," its i'rab (grammatical case inflection) follows it, as is said in "a hole of a lizard, ruined" and similar expressions. This is a likeness that God struck for the deeds of the disbeliever, meaning: they gain nothing from their deeds that they performed in the world, because they associated partners with God in them, just as the ashes that the wind scatters are of no benefit. This is His saying ﴿they have no power over anything they have earned﴾, meaning the disbelievers, from what they earned in the world, over anything in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the far-off error.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth﴾.

The people of Kufa, except Amir, read *khāliq al-samāwāti wal-arḍ* (Creator of the heavens and the earth), as an emphatic form (of the active participle, on the pattern of *fāʿil*). See al-Tabari's commentary: 13/260.

The others read *khalaqa al-samāwāti* (He created the heavens), in the sense of ﴿with truth﴾. The exegetes said: He did not create them in vain, but He created them for a great purpose.

﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation﴾: He will replace you with what is better, more excellent, and more obedient than you. ﴿That is not difficult for God﴾: it is not unattainable or impossible for Him. ﴿And they will all appear before God﴾: they will come out of their graves and be made manifest before God, all of them. The verb is in the future. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾: meaning the followers say to the leaders who were followed: ﴿We were your followers﴾. *Tabaʿ* is the plural of *tābiʿ* (follower), like *ḥāris* and *ḥaras* (guard, guards). It has also been said: *rāṣid* and *rasad* (watcher, watchers), and *nāfir* and *nafr* (one who flees, those who flee). It is also permissible for *tabaʿ* to be a verbal noun that was used as a name, meaning "we were people of following." See al-Qurtubi's commentary: 9/355.

﴿Can you then relieve us of anything from the punishment of God?﴾, meaning: can you, together with your ... , ward off God's punishment from us? The leaders say: ﴿If God had guided us, we would have guided you﴾, up to His saying ﴿no place of escape﴾: no refuge and no escape. It may be both a verbal noun and a noun. It is said: *ḥāṣa fulān ʿan kadhā*, meaning he fled and turned away from it, *yaḥīṣu ḥaysan* and *ḥiyūṣan* and *ḥiyṣānan*.

Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire, "Come, let us lament," and they will lament for five hundred years, and the lamenting will not benefit them. They will say, "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for five hundred years, and the patience will not benefit them. Then they will say: ﴿It is the same for us whether we lament or are patient; we have no place of escape.﴾

﴿And the Satan will say﴾, meaning Iblis, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning when the matter has been finished: the people of Paradise have been admitted to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

Muqatil said: a pulpit of fire will be placed for him, and he will climb it, and the disbelievers will gather around him with their leaders. ﴿God promised you the promise of truth﴾, which will be fulfilled for you. ﴿And I promised you, and I broke it. I had no authority over you﴾, meaning no dominion, no kingdom, no proof, and no insight. ﴿Except that I called you﴾: this is an exception of a disconnected kind (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*), whose meaning is: except for those who called you. ﴿So you responded to me. Do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ for responding to me and following me without authority and without proof. ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾: I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper, I will not give you relief nor you me.

The common readers read *bi-muṣrikhiyya* with a fatha on the *yāʾ*. Al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read it with a kasra on the *yāʾ*. The original form is *bi-muṣrikhiyyīn*: the *nūn* was dropped because of the possessive construction, and the *yāʾ* of the plural was assimilated into the *yāʾ* of the first person possessive. Whoever reads with a fatha does so because of the doubling, and whoever reads with a kasra does so because two unvocalized letters came together, so it was vocalized with a kasra, since the *yāʾ* is a sister of the kasra. See al-Qurtubi: 9/357.

﴿I disbelieve in your having associated me with God before﴾: that is, it is not possible for me to be a partner to God in what you associated me with through your obedience to me. I mock that. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers, the disbelievers who place obedience to creatures where it does not belong, will have a painful punishment.﴾

Utbah ibn Amir narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith about intercession, that he said: "Jesus (peace be upon him) will say: 'Go to that unlettered Prophet, and they will come to me, and God will permit me to rise, and my assembly will be stirred up with the most fragrant scent anyone has smelled, until I come and he intercedes for me, and places for me a light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot.'"

Then the disbelievers will say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them; so who will intercede for us?" They will say: "There is no one but Iblis, he is the one who led us astray." They will come and say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so get up and intercede for us, for you led us astray." He will say: he rises from his assembly, and a stench rises from it that is the most foul anyone has smelled. Then their wailing will grow intense, and at that moment he will say: ﴿God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke it﴾ [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/327; Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/263.]].

...﴿And those who believed will be admitted﴾, up to His saying ﴿therein is peace﴾: God will greet them with peace, and the angels will greet them with peace.

﴿Do you not see, O Muhammad?﴾, meaning: God knows, through my informing you, ﴿how God struck a likeness: a good word﴾, meaning God has clarified its likeness: a good word, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿like a good tree﴾, which is the date palm. This is shown by the hadith of Utayb al-Hijab, who said: Abu al-Aliyah was my guardian (*amīn*). One day he came to me at my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I went with him to Anas ibn Malik. I entered upon him, and a tray with fresh dates was brought.

Anas said: "Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree that God mentioned in His Book: ﴿Do you not see how God struck a likeness: a good word, like a good tree﴾." Then Anas said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was brought a basket of unripe dates, and he recited this verse."

The meaning of the verse is: like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of the fruit is omitted because the food indicates it.

Abu Dhabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: "This is a tree in Paradise, ﴿whose root is firm in the earth, and whose branches are high in the sky﴾. Likewise, the root of this word is established in the heart of the believer through knowledge, affirmation, and sincerity. When he speaks the testimony, it ascends to the sky, and it is not recorded until it reaches God, the Exalted. God said: ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and righteous deeds raise it﴾ [[Surah Fatir: 10.]]."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has a pillar of light whose base is beneath the seventh earth and whose top is beneath the Throne. When the servant says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' that pillar trembles, and God, mighty and majestic, says: 'Be still!' It says: 'How can I be still, when You have not forgiven the one who said it?' The Lord says: 'I have forgiven him,' and then it is still."

The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "Increase your shaking of that pillar" [[Al-Mawdu'at of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/167; Majma' al-Zawa'id, abridged: 10/82.]].

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾, meaning it gives its fruit. The commentators differed about *ḥīn* (season).

Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zayd said: every year.

Ikrimah said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "I vowed to cut off a man's hand from such-and-such a year and season; what is your opinion about it?" Ibn Abbas said: I said to him: "Do not cut off his hand; imprison him for a year" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/274.]].

Indeed Ibn Abbas says: *ḥīn* has two kinds: a season that is known and changes, and a season that is not known. As for the unknown season: ﴿and you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [[Surah Sad: 88.]]. As for the known one: ﴿it gives its fruit every season﴾, which is the period from one year to the next.

Umar said: "You are right, O client of Ibn Abbas, and you have done well" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Nahhas, abridged: 3/528.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and al-Hasan said: every six months, from its *ʿarām* (the first blossoming, the sprouting of the spathe) to its bearing.

Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about a man who swore not to speak to his brother for a *ḥīn*. He said: "The *ḥīn* is seven months," and he recited this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The *ḥīn* is two months, because the palm does not have its fruit except for two months."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿every season﴾ means every morning and evening; likewise the deed of the believer rises at the beginning of the day and at its end. This is also the narration of Abu Dhabyan from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Dahhak said: every hour, by night and by day, in winter and in summer; it is eaten at all times. Likewise the believer is never without good at all times.

Abu al-Hakam recited the likeness of faith to the tree: a tree is not a tree except through three things: a firm trunk, a standing root, and high branches. Likewise faith is not complete and does not stand except through three things: affirmation by the heart, speech by the tongue, and action by the body.

This is supported by what Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Faith is affirmation by the heart, acknowledgment by the tongue, and action by the limbs" [[Hadith no. 160.]].

Humayd al-Tawil narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the likeness of this religion is that of a firm tree: faith is its root, zakat is its branch, fasting is its roots, calling to God is its shoots, good character is its leaves, and refraining from what God has forbidden is its greenness. Just as this tree is not perfected except by good fruit, faith is not perfected except by refraining from what God has forbidden" [[Hadith no. 161; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]].

The wisdom in its likening faith to the palm among all other trees is that, since it is the most similar of trees to a human being, it was likened to him. For every tree, when its top is cut off, branches out from its sides, but the palm, when its top is cut off, dries up and its root perishes. Also, it resembles a human being and other animals in pollination, since it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best wealth is a pollinated palm-row and a well-tended mount" [[Hadith no. 162; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/270.]].

Among this is the hadith of Ibn Umar: the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "There is a tree among trees whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is." People began to name the trees of the desert, but it came to my mind that it was the palm, then I looked and I was the youngest of the people, so I was too shy and kept silent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm" [[Hadith no. 163.]]. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "O my son, if you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than such-and-such," because it is from the tree of Adam [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 1/481, no. 12460.]].

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Honor your aunt." It was said: "And who is our aunt, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The palm" [[Hadith no. 164; Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/338, no. 35300; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]]. This is because when God created Adam, a portion of his clay was set aside, and from it He created the palm. God said: ﴿God strikes the likenesses for people, that they may remember﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 25.]]. ﴿And the likeness of a corrupt word﴾, which is shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿is like a corrupt tree﴾, which is the colocynth.

Ibn Abbas said: this is a likeness that God struck, and He did not create this tree on the face of the earth.

﴿Uprooted﴾: pulled up. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "loosened." Al-Dahhak said: "cut off from the roots." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "it is taken wherever it is, with certainty." ﴿From above the earth; it has no stability.﴾ Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word ascends from him, nor righteous deed.

﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾: God confirms their faith and their deeds through the word and the making firm, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ Meaning in the grave; and it has been said: "in the life of this world" means in the grave, in the sight of God, the Exalted, and "in the Hereafter" means when they are resurrected.

Muqatil said: this is because when the believer dies, God sends to him an angel called Ruman, who enters his grave and says to him: "There will come to you now two black angels who will ask you: Who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, and who are your leaders? Answer them with what you were upon in your life." Then he (Ruman) leaves, and the two angels enter, Munkar and Nakir, black and blue, harsh and coarse, their eyes like flashing lightning and their voices like a violent wind, with maces. They sit him up and question him, and they do not notice the entry of Ruman. He says: "My Lord is God, my Prophet is Muhammad, and my religion is Islam." They say to him: "Blessed by God," then they say: "O God, please him as You pleased Yourself." A door of Paradise is opened for him in his grave, from which gifts come to him. When they leave him, he is told: "Sleep the sleep of the bride." This is the making firm. ﴿And God leads the wrongdoers astray﴾, meaning He curses them. When the disbeliever is visited by the two angels, they say to him: "Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not know and you were not guided; you lived in rebellion and died in wretchedness." Then they say to him: "Sleep the sleep of one who is struck," and a door of Hell is opened for him from his grave, and they strike him with that mace, and he shrieks a shriek that every creature hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), and every one who hears his voice curses him. This is His saying ﴿and those who curse will curse them﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 159.]].

Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the believer's soul, and said: "His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' They rebuke him and say a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' This is the last of the angels' questions, and God makes him firm, so he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out in the sky: 'Make My servant firm.'" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281; Musnad Ahmad: 4/287, with slight variation.]] Then the saying of God was revealed: ﴿God makes firm those who believe﴾, the verse.

Ibn Abbas said concerning this verse: when death attends the believer, the angels witness it, greet him with peace, and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he sits up in his grave, and he is asked: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is God." He is asked: "Who is your messenger?" He says: "Muhammad." He is asked: "What is your testimony?" He says: "I testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then his grave is widened as far as his eye can see. This is His saying ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Abu Nadrah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his beloved ones disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mallet in his hand and seats him up and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he is a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The angel says to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wants to rise toward it, but he is told: 'Be still.' Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, you did not recite, and you were not guided.'
