Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel strikes him with the mallet, a blow that every creature of God hears except the two weighty ones."

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is none among us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer (mitraq) without being terrified by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah makes firm those who believe" [verse 27]. [166] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/637, no. 42509; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281.]]

Abu Hurayrah said: "The deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer would be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the good deeds—charity, kinship ties and kindness—would be at his feet. People would pray over him, and then he would be approached from the direction of his head, and it would say, 'Prayer, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his right, and it would say, 'Zakat, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his left, and it would say, 'Fasting, come forward,' and it would enter. Then his voice would come from the direction of his feet, and it would say, 'Good deeds, come forward,' and it would enter. He would be told, 'Sit up,' and he would sit up, the sun having been depicted to him and the time of sunset having arrived. He would be told, 'Tell us what we ask you.' He would say, 'Leave me until I pray.' It would be said, 'You will indeed do so. Tell us what we ask you about.' He would say, 'What do you want to ask me?' They would say, 'What do you think of this man who was among you, and what did he testify to?' He would say, 'Muhammad?' They would say, 'Yes.' He would say, 'I testify that he is truly the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him.' It would be said to him, 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then his grave would be widened for him to seventy cubits and it would be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has prepared for you therein,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has averted from you had you disobeyed Him,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then his soul would be placed in a pleasant breeze, and it is a green bird hanging from the trees of Paradise, and his body would be returned to the dust from which it was created. This is the meaning of His saying: 'Allah makes firm those who believe' [verse 27] up to His saying, 'and in the Hereafter' [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/283.]]."

And on the authority of Abu Nafi' who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking by a pool of water, and I was walking behind him, he (ﷺ) said: 'May you not be guided, may you not be guided,' three times." [167] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/325.]]

Abu Nafi' said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with me?' He said: 'I did not mean you; I mean the owner of this grave. He will be asked about me, and he will claim that he does not know me.' It was a grave that had been sprinkled with water when its occupant was buried."

Abu al-Qasim al-Sulami informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Khayyat, who said: I heard Suhayl ibn Jabir al-'Ataki say: "I saw Yazid ibn 'Uthman in a dream after his death, and I asked him, 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Two angels came to me in my grave, harsh and coarse, and said, "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" I seized my white beard and said to them, "Is this how someone like me is addressed, when I have known the people's answer to your question for eighty years?" They left and said, "Did you write down from Jarir ibn 'Uthman?" I said, "Yes." They said, "He used to hate 'Ali, so Allah hated him."' " [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/363.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 18–27 (part 1 of 2):

﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 18.]]. The grammarians differed over the nominative case of *mathal* (likeness). Al-Farra' said: the likeness is attributed to those who disbelieve, while the likeness itself belongs to the deeds, because the Arabs put the nouns first since they are more definite, and then bring the predicate that is stated about them together with their referent. The meaning of the verse is: the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is like ashes. Compare His saying ﴿He who perfected everything He created﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 7.]], meaning: He perfected the creation of everything. And His saying ﴿On the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against God, their faces blackened﴾ [[Surah al-Zumar: 60.]], meaning: on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied against God blackened, evilly blackened. In the verse there is an implied element, whose meaning is: and the likeness of those who disbelieve in their Lord is not to be recited to you. Then it begins, and he proceeds to explain it, saying: "their deeds are like ashes."

If you wish, you may make *mathal* an attribute and say: "Those who disbelieve in their Lord—their deeds are like ashes ﴿which the wind blows violently on a stormy day﴾." The day is described as stormy, though stormy is a property of the wind, because the wind occurs on it, just as one says "a cold day" or "a hot day," since cold and heat occur in it; and "a sleeping night" and "a fasting day." God said ﴿and the day as one that makes things visible﴾ [[Surah Yunus: 67.]], and the night and the day indicate this. The poet said:

*Two cloudy days and one sunny day*

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

Al-Farra' also said: if you wish, you may say "on a day of stormy wind" (*fi yawm ʿasūf*), and if you wish, you may say "on a day of wind that is stormy" (*fi yawm ʿāṣif al-rīḥ*), omitting "the wind" because it has been mentioned before. This is like the poet's saying:

*When a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed*

[[Lisan al-Arab: 9/248; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/258.]]

meaning: the sun is eclipsed (*kasif al-shams*).

It has also been said that it is an attribute of the wind, but since it came after "day," its i'rab (grammatical case inflection) follows it, as is said in "a hole of a lizard, ruined" and similar expressions. This is a likeness that God struck for the deeds of the disbeliever, meaning: they gain nothing from their deeds that they performed in the world, because they associated partners with God in them, just as the ashes that the wind scatters are of no benefit. This is His saying ﴿they have no power over anything they have earned﴾, meaning the disbelievers, from what they earned in the world, over anything in the Hereafter. ﴿That is the far-off error.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that God created the heavens and the earth﴾.

The people of Kufa, except Amir, read *khāliq al-samāwāti wal-arḍ* (Creator of the heavens and the earth), as an emphatic form (of the active participle, on the pattern of *fāʿil*). See al-Tabari's commentary: 13/260.

The others read *khalaqa al-samāwāti* (He created the heavens), in the sense of ﴿with truth﴾. The exegetes said: He did not create them in vain, but He created them for a great purpose.

﴿If He wills, He will remove you and bring a new creation﴾: He will replace you with what is better, more excellent, and more obedient than you. ﴿That is not difficult for God﴾: it is not unattainable or impossible for Him. ﴿And they will all appear before God﴾: they will come out of their graves and be made manifest before God, all of them. The verb is in the future. ﴿The weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾: meaning the followers say to the leaders who were followed: ﴿We were your followers﴾. *Tabaʿ* is the plural of *tābiʿ* (follower), like *ḥāris* and *ḥaras* (guard, guards). It has also been said: *rāṣid* and *rasad* (watcher, watchers), and *nāfir* and *nafr* (one who flees, those who flee). It is also permissible for *tabaʿ* to be a verbal noun that was used as a name, meaning "we were people of following." See al-Qurtubi's commentary: 9/355.

﴿Can you then relieve us of anything from the punishment of God?﴾, meaning: can you, together with your ... , ward off God's punishment from us? The leaders say: ﴿If God had guided us, we would have guided you﴾, up to His saying ﴿no place of escape﴾: no refuge and no escape. It may be both a verbal noun and a noun. It is said: *ḥāṣa fulān ʿan kadhā*, meaning he fled and turned away from it, *yaḥīṣu ḥaysan* and *ḥiyūṣan* and *ḥiyṣānan*.

Muqatil said: They will say in the Fire, "Come, let us lament," and they will lament for five hundred years, and the lamenting will not benefit them. They will say, "Come, let us be patient," and they will be patient for five hundred years, and the patience will not benefit them. Then they will say: ﴿It is the same for us whether we lament or are patient; we have no place of escape.﴾

﴿And the Satan will say﴾, meaning Iblis, ﴿when the matter has been decided﴾, meaning when the matter has been finished: the people of Paradise have been admitted to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

Muqatil said: a pulpit of fire will be placed for him, and he will climb it, and the disbelievers will gather around him with their leaders. ﴿God promised you the promise of truth﴾, which will be fulfilled for you. ﴿And I promised you, and I broke it. I had no authority over you﴾, meaning no dominion, no kingdom, no proof, and no insight. ﴿Except that I called you﴾: this is an exception of a disconnected kind (*istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ*), whose meaning is: except for those who called you. ﴿So you responded to me. Do not blame me, but blame yourselves﴾ for responding to me and following me without authority and without proof. ﴿I cannot help you, nor can you help me﴾: I cannot be your helper, nor can you be my helper, I will not give you relief nor you me.

The common readers read *bi-muṣrikhiyya* with a fatha on the *yāʾ*. Al-Aʿmash and Hamzah read it with a kasra on the *yāʾ*. The original form is *bi-muṣrikhiyyīn*: the *nūn* was dropped because of the possessive construction, and the *yāʾ* of the plural was assimilated into the *yāʾ* of the first person possessive. Whoever reads with a fatha does so because of the doubling, and whoever reads with a kasra does so because two unvocalized letters came together, so it was vocalized with a kasra, since the *yāʾ* is a sister of the kasra. See al-Qurtubi: 9/357.

﴿I disbelieve in your having associated me with God before﴾: that is, it is not possible for me to be a partner to God in what you associated me with through your obedience to me. I mock that. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers, the disbelievers who place obedience to creatures where it does not belong, will have a painful punishment.﴾

Utbah ibn Amir narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith about intercession, that he said: "Jesus (peace be upon him) will say: 'Go to that unlettered Prophet, and they will come to me, and God will permit me to rise, and my assembly will be stirred up with the most fragrant scent anyone has smelled, until I come and he intercedes for me, and places for me a light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot.'"

Then the disbelievers will say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them; so who will intercede for us?" They will say: "There is no one but Iblis, he is the one who led us astray." They will come and say: "The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so get up and intercede for us, for you led us astray." He will say: he rises from his assembly, and a stench rises from it that is the most foul anyone has smelled. Then their wailing will grow intense, and at that moment he will say: ﴿God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke it﴾ [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/327; Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/263.]].

...﴿And those who believed will be admitted﴾, up to His saying ﴿therein is peace﴾: God will greet them with peace, and the angels will greet them with peace.

﴿Do you not see, O Muhammad?﴾, meaning: God knows, through my informing you, ﴿how God struck a likeness: a good word﴾, meaning God has clarified its likeness: a good word, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿like a good tree﴾, which is the date palm. This is shown by the hadith of Utayb al-Hijab, who said: Abu al-Aliyah was my guardian (*amīn*). One day he came to me at my house after I had prayed the dawn prayer, and I went with him to Anas ibn Malik. I entered upon him, and a tray with fresh dates was brought.

Anas said: "Eat, O Abu al-Aliyah, for this is from the tree that God mentioned in His Book: ﴿Do you not see how God struck a likeness: a good word, like a good tree﴾." Then Anas said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was brought a basket of unripe dates, and he recited this verse."

The meaning of the verse is: like a tree good in its fruit. The mention of the fruit is omitted because the food indicates it.

Abu Dhabyan narrated from Ibn Abbas: "This is a tree in Paradise, ﴿whose root is firm in the earth, and whose branches are high in the sky﴾. Likewise, the root of this word is established in the heart of the believer through knowledge, affirmation, and sincerity. When he speaks the testimony, it ascends to the sky, and it is not recorded until it reaches God, the Exalted. God said: ﴿To Him ascend the good word, and righteous deeds raise it﴾ [[Surah Fatir: 10.]]."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God has a pillar of light whose base is beneath the seventh earth and whose top is beneath the Throne. When the servant says, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' that pillar trembles, and God, mighty and majestic, says: 'Be still!' It says: 'How can I be still, when You have not forgiven the one who said it?' The Lord says: 'I have forgiven him,' and then it is still."

The Prophet (ﷺ) then said: "Increase your shaking of that pillar" [[Al-Mawdu'at of Ibn al-Jawzi: 3/167; Majma' al-Zawa'id, abridged: 10/82.]].

﴿It gives its fruit every season﴾, meaning it gives its fruit. The commentators differed about *ḥīn* (season).

Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ibn Zayd said: every year.

Ikrimah said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: "I vowed to cut off a man's hand from such-and-such a year and season; what is your opinion about it?" Ibn Abbas said: I said to him: "Do not cut off his hand; imprison him for a year" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/274.]].

Indeed Ibn Abbas says: *ḥīn* has two kinds: a season that is known and changes, and a season that is not known. As for the unknown season: ﴿and you will surely know its news after a time﴾ [[Surah Sad: 88.]]. As for the known one: ﴿it gives its fruit every season﴾, which is the period from one year to the next.

Umar said: "You are right, O client of Ibn Abbas, and you have done well" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Nahhas, abridged: 3/528.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, and al-Hasan said: every six months, from its *ʿarām* (the first blossoming, the sprouting of the spathe) to its bearing.

Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about a man who swore not to speak to his brother for a *ḥīn*. He said: "The *ḥīn* is seven months," and he recited this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The *ḥīn* is two months, because the palm does not have its fruit except for two months."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿every season﴾ means every morning and evening; likewise the deed of the believer rises at the beginning of the day and at its end. This is also the narration of Abu Dhabyan from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Dahhak said: every hour, by night and by day, in winter and in summer; it is eaten at all times. Likewise the believer is never without good at all times.

Abu al-Hakam recited the likeness of faith to the tree: a tree is not a tree except through three things: a firm trunk, a standing root, and high branches. Likewise faith is not complete and does not stand except through three things: affirmation by the heart, speech by the tongue, and action by the body.

This is supported by what Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Faith is affirmation by the heart, acknowledgment by the tongue, and action by the limbs" [[Hadith no. 160.]].

Humayd al-Tawil narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the likeness of this religion is that of a firm tree: faith is its root, zakat is its branch, fasting is its roots, calling to God is its shoots, good character is its leaves, and refraining from what God has forbidden is its greenness. Just as this tree is not perfected except by good fruit, faith is not perfected except by refraining from what God has forbidden" [[Hadith no. 161; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]].

The wisdom in its likening faith to the palm among all other trees is that, since it is the most similar of trees to a human being, it was likened to him. For every tree, when its top is cut off, branches out from its sides, but the palm, when its top is cut off, dries up and its root perishes. Also, it resembles a human being and other animals in pollination, since it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best wealth is a pollinated palm-row and a well-tended mount" [[Hadith no. 162; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/270.]].

Among this is the hadith of Ibn Umar: the Prophet (ﷺ) said one day to his companions: "There is a tree among trees whose leaves do not fall, and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is." People began to name the trees of the desert, but it came to my mind that it was the palm, then I looked and I was the youngest of the people, so I was too shy and kept silent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is the palm" [[Hadith no. 163.]]. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "O my son, if you had said it, it would have been dearer to me than such-and-such," because it is from the tree of Adam [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 1/481, no. 12460.]].

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Honor your aunt." It was said: "And who is our aunt, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The palm" [[Hadith no. 164; Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/338, no. 35300; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/360.]]. This is because when God created Adam, a portion of his clay was set aside, and from it He created the palm. God said: ﴿God strikes the likenesses for people, that they may remember﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 25.]]. ﴿And the likeness of a corrupt word﴾, which is shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿is like a corrupt tree﴾, which is the colocynth.

Ibn Abbas said: this is a likeness that God struck, and He did not create this tree on the face of the earth.

﴿Uprooted﴾: pulled up. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: "loosened." Al-Dahhak said: "cut off from the roots." Al-Mu'arrikh said: "it is taken wherever it is, with certainty." ﴿From above the earth; it has no stability.﴾ Likewise the disbeliever has no good in him, and no good word ascends from him, nor righteous deed.

﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word﴾: God confirms their faith and their deeds through the word and the making firm, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ Meaning in the grave; and it has been said: "in the life of this world" means in the grave, in the sight of God, the Exalted, and "in the Hereafter" means when they are resurrected.

Muqatil said: this is because when the believer dies, God sends to him an angel called Ruman, who enters his grave and says to him: "There will come to you now two black angels who will ask you: Who is your Lord, who is your Prophet, and who are your leaders? Answer them with what you were upon in your life." Then he (Ruman) leaves, and the two angels enter, Munkar and Nakir, black and blue, harsh and coarse, their eyes like flashing lightning and their voices like a violent wind, with maces. They sit him up and question him, and they do not notice the entry of Ruman. He says: "My Lord is God, my Prophet is Muhammad, and my religion is Islam." They say to him: "Blessed by God," then they say: "O God, please him as You pleased Yourself." A door of Paradise is opened for him in his grave, from which gifts come to him. When they leave him, he is told: "Sleep the sleep of the bride." This is the making firm. ﴿And God leads the wrongdoers astray﴾, meaning He curses them. When the disbeliever is visited by the two angels, they say to him: "Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not know and you were not guided; you lived in rebellion and died in wretchedness." Then they say to him: "Sleep the sleep of one who is struck," and a door of Hell is opened for him from his grave, and they strike him with that mace, and he shrieks a shriek that every creature hears except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), and every one who hears his voice curses him. This is His saying ﴿and those who curse will curse them﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 159.]].

Al-Bara' ibn Azib narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mentioned the taking of the believer's soul, and said: "His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him in his grave, and they say: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' He says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad.' They rebuke him and say a second time: 'Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet?' This is the last of the angels' questions, and God makes him firm, so he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then a caller calls out in the sky: 'Make My servant firm.'" [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281; Musnad Ahmad: 4/287, with slight variation.]] Then the saying of God was revealed: ﴿God makes firm those who believe﴾, the verse.

Ibn Abbas said concerning this verse: when death attends the believer, the angels witness it, greet him with peace, and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he sits up in his grave, and he is asked: "Who is your Lord?" He says: "My Lord is God." He is asked: "Who is your messenger?" He says: "Muhammad." He is asked: "What is your testimony?" He says: "I testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God." Then his grave is widened as far as his eye can see. This is His saying ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Abu Nadrah narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at a funeral, and he said: "O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his beloved ones disperse from him, an angel comes to him with a mallet in his hand and seats him up and says: 'What do you say about this man?' If he is a believer, he says: 'I testify that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The angel says to him: 'You have spoken the truth.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you disbelieved in your Lord; but since you believed in Him, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wants to rise toward it, but he is told: 'Be still.' Then his grave is widened for him. As for the disbeliever or the hypocrite, it is said to him: 'What do you say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You did not know, you did not recite, and you were not guided.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'This was your dwelling had you believed in your Lord; but since you disbelieved, God has exchanged it for you for this.' Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and then the angel strikes him with the mallet, a blow that every creature of God hears except the two weighty ones."

Some of his companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, there is none among us over whose head an angel stands holding a hammer (mitraq) without being terrified by it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah makes firm those who believe" [verse 27]. [166] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/637, no. 42509; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 13/281.]]

Abu Hurayrah said: "The deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer would be at his head, zakat at his right, fasting at his left, and the good deeds—charity, kinship ties and kindness—would be at his feet. People would pray over him, and then he would be approached from the direction of his head, and it would say, 'Prayer, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his right, and it would say, 'Zakat, come forward,' and it would enter. Then he would be approached from his left, and it would say, 'Fasting, come forward,' and it would enter. Then his voice would come from the direction of his feet, and it would say, 'Good deeds, come forward,' and it would enter. He would be told, 'Sit up,' and he would sit up, the sun having been depicted to him and the time of sunset having arrived. He would be told, 'Tell us what we ask you.' He would say, 'Leave me until I pray.' It would be said, 'You will indeed do so. Tell us what we ask you about.' He would say, 'What do you want to ask me?' They would say, 'What do you think of this man who was among you, and what did he testify to?' He would say, 'Muhammad?' They would say, 'Yes.' He would say, 'I testify that he is truly the Messenger of Allah; he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, and we believed him.' It would be said to him, 'Upon that you lived, upon that you died, and upon that you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.' Then his grave would be widened for him to seventy cubits and it would be illuminated for him. Then a door to Paradise would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has prepared for you therein,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then a door to the Fire would be opened for him, and it would be said to him, 'Look at what Allah has averted from you had you disobeyed Him,' and he would increase in joy and delight. Then his soul would be placed in a pleasant breeze, and it is a green bird hanging from the trees of Paradise, and his body would be returned to the dust from which it was created. This is the meaning of His saying: 'Allah makes firm those who believe' [verse 27] up to His saying, 'and in the Hereafter' [[in full in Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/283.]]."

And on the authority of Abu Nafi' who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was walking by a pool of water, and I was walking behind him, he (ﷺ) said: 'May you not be guided, may you not be guided,' three times." [167] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 1/325.]]

Abu Nafi' said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is wrong with me?' He said: 'I did not mean you; I mean the owner of this grave. He will be asked about me, and he will claim that he does not know me.' It was a grave that had been sprinkled with water when its occupant was buried."

Abu al-Qasim al-Sulami informed us, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Khayyat, who said: I heard Suhayl ibn Jabir al-'Ataki say: "I saw Yazid ibn 'Uthman in a dream after his death, and I asked him, 'What did Allah do with you?' He said: 'Two angels came to me in my grave, harsh and coarse, and said, "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?" I seized my white beard and said to them, "Is this how someone like me is addressed, when I have known the people's answer to your question for eighty years?" They left and said, "Did you write down from Jarir ibn 'Uthman?" I said, "Yes." They said, "He used to hate 'Ali, so Allah hated him."' " [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/363.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verse 28–34:

﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for ingratitude and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin?﴾ Meaning: they changed the favour of Allah upon them by denying Muhammad (ﷺ) when Allah sent him from among them and to them, so they disbelieved in him and denied him, and thus they turned the favour of Allah upon them into disbelief. ﴿And caused their people to settle﴾ means: they made to descend and settle their people, those who followed them in their disbelief, ﴿in the abode of ruin﴾, meaning destruction. Then [he was asked](Added from Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/287.) about what the abode of ruin is, and he said: ﴿Hell, which they will enter, and it is an evil place to settle﴾, meaning the dwelling place (al-mustaqarr).

Amir ibn Wathila said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) say, concerning His words ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged...﴾ [the verse], that they are the disbelievers of Quraysh who were slaughtered on the day of Badr. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/364.)

Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: They are the two wicked ones of Quraysh, the Banu Umayya and the Banu Makhzum. As for the Banu Umayya, they were given enjoyment for a while, and as for the Banu Makhzum, they were destroyed on the day of Badr. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/364, where he attributes it to both Umar and Ali.)

Ibn Abbas: They are the Christianized Arabs, Jabala ibn al-Ayham and his companions. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/364.)

﴿And they set up rivals to Allah in order to mislead [from His way]﴾. The Kufans read *liyudilla* with a damma on the yā' (*liyuḍillū*), meaning "to mislead people from His way," while the rest read it with a fatha on the yā' (*liyaḍillū*), by way of necessity (lazum), i.e., their end was misguidance and going astray; this is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). ﴿Say: Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire﴾, meaning: live the enjoyment of worldly life. ﴿Indeed, your destination is to the Fire﴾; this is a warning.

His words: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: they should establish prayer﴾. Al-Farra' said: regarding the vowel of *yuqīmū* (they should establish): there are several aspects to this. One of them, and it was said that it is by omitting the imperative lam, meaning *liyuqīmū* (let them establish); and it was said that it is the answer to the imperative, which is "say." Its jussive form, *yuqīmū*, is by way of interpreting it as a conditional, and its meaning is a command. (Added from Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/294; the manuscript's wording is garbled.)

﴿And spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, before a Day in which there is no trade or friendship (khilal)﴾. It is said: *khallaltu fulanan*, so I take him as a close friend (akhāluhu mukhālatan), and *khullah* and *khilal*.

Imru' al-Qays said:

*I turned my desire away from them out of fear of destruction, and I took as a friend one who is disdained, and was not one who disdains.* (Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/294.)

﴿Allah is the One who created the heavens...﴾ [the verse] up to His words ﴿the sun and the moon, both continuing [in their courses]﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: their continuous motion in obedience to Allah.

﴿And He subjected to you the night and the day﴾, alternating in light and darkness, and in decrease and increase. ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾. Meaning: He gave you of everything you asked of Him, some thing, so the second object is omitted, relying on the context to indicate partiality, like His words ﴿and she has been given of everything﴾ (Surah al-Naml: 23), meaning: she has been given some of everything in her time. It was also said that it indicates abundance, like your saying: "So-and-so knows everything," and "all the people came to him," while you mean some of them. Its parallel is His words ﴿We opened to them the gates of everything﴾ (Surah al-An'am: 44).

Some exegetes said: the meaning is "He gave you of all that you asked of Him and what you did not ask Him." This is the common reading with the genitive (idafa) [.........] [an illegible word.]

Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Salam read *min kullin*, with tanwin, as a negation, meaning: of everything that you did not ask Him for, so that *ma* is a relative pronoun.

Al-Dahhak said: He gave you things you did not request nor ask for. Allah spoke the truth: of whatever Allah gave us, we did not ask Him for it, nor did it occur to our minds. (Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/297.)

﴿And if you were to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾, meaning: you cannot bear to mention it, nor to perform its thanks, neither with the heart, nor with the tongue, nor with eloquence. ﴿Indeed, mankind is truly wrongdoing, ungrateful﴾: wrongdoing, meaning one who is thankful to other than the One who bestowed the favour upon him, placing gratitude in other than its proper place; ungrateful, meaning one who denies the blessings of Allah. It was said: wrongdoing to himself by his disobedience; ungrateful to his Lord regarding His blessing. It was also said: wrongdoing in hardship, complaining and despairing; ungrateful in ease, hoarding and withholding.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 14, verses 35–41:**

﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this city secure"﴾, meaning the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), made safe within it. ﴿And keep me and my sons away﴾ from ﴿worshipping idols﴾. It is said: "jannabtuhu, ajnubuhu, janban," and "ajnabtuhu, ijnaban," with the same meaning, and "ajnabuka" and "jannabtuhu, tajniban."

The poet said, and he is Umayyah ibn al-Ashkar al-Laythi:

*"She shakes his cradle out of compassion for him,
and keeps him away, so he does not endure hardships."*

"Idols" (al-asnam) is the plural of "sanam," which is a sculpted image. The poet said:

*"A slender woman, like a palm-branch, shows her inner beauty,
she laughs, revealing sweet, clear-white teeth."*

Ibrahim al-Taymi said in his stories: "Who can feel safe from trial after Abraham, the Friend of God (peace be upon him), when he says: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾" meaning that many people went astray through them, to the point that they worshipped them. This is from the inverted usage (al-maghlub). Its parallel is His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿Whoever follows me is indeed of me﴾, upon my religion and my creed, ﴿and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Al-Suddi said: its meaning is ﴿and whoever disobeys me﴾, so that he repents.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿and whoever disobeys me﴾ refers to anything short of association (shirk).

Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited the words of Abraham (peace be upon him): ﴿Whoever follows me is indeed of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

And the words of Jesus (peace be upon him): ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾ [Qur'an 5:118], the verse, and he raised his hands and said: "O God, my community! O God, my community!" and wept. God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what is wrong with him." So Gabriel came and asked him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told him what he had said. God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: 'We shall indeed please you regarding your community, and will not grieve you.'"

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring﴾. What is inserted here, "min" (some of), is for partition, and the meaning of the verse is: I have settled some of my offspring, a son, ﴿in an uncultivated valley﴾, which is Mecca, ﴿near Your Sacred House﴾.

Qatadah said: "The Sacred House is sacred because God has made it inviolable, and disrespecting its right is forbidden." If it is asked, what is the meaning of Abraham's words "near Your House," when Abraham built the House only a long time afterward? It is said the meaning is "near Your Sacred House," which existed before He raised it from the earth, until it was raised in the days of the Flood.

It is also said: "near Your Sacred House" means the House that had already been decreed in Your knowledge, that it would come to be in this land.

The story of the verse, as related by Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, is that Ibn Abbas said: "The first to run between al-Safa and al-Marwah was Hajar, the mother of Isma'il. And the first thing that was introduced was the dragging of garments, for Hajar did that, because when she fled from Sarah she let down her garment so her footprints would be hidden. Abraham brought her and her son Isma'il until he brought them to the place of the House, and he set them down and turned back. She said: 'To whom are you leaving us?' He did not answer her at all. So she said: 'Did God command you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not let us be lost.' So she turned back, and [Abraham] went on, until when he reached the pass of Kada he faced the valley and said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley﴾, the verse." [Sahih al-Bukhari 4/114].

He said: With the woman was a waterskin containing water, and the water ran out, so she became thirsty, and her milk dried up, and the child became thirsty. She looked at the mountains nearest to the ground, and climbed al-Safa, and listened carefully to see whether she could hear a voice or see anyone, but she heard nothing. So she came down, and when she reached the valley she ran, like a person exhausted who runs without intending to run. Then she looked for the nearest mountain to the ground, climbed al-Marwah, listened carefully to hear a voice or see someone. She heard a voice and said, like a person whose hearing deceives him: "Be quiet," until she was certain. Then she said: "You have made me hear your voice, so help me, for I am lost and whoever is with me is lost." Then there was the angel, who came with her until he brought her to the place of Zamzam, struck the ground with his foot, and a spring gushed forth. The woman hurried and began to pour it into her waterskin.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. If she had not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring." The angel said to her: "Do not fear thirst for the people of this land, for this is a spring for the drink of God's guests," and he said: "The father of this boy will come, and they will build a House for God, this is its place."

He said: A caravan from Jurhum passed by, heading for Syria. They saw birds over the mountain, and said: "These birds are circling over water." They came up and saw the woman, so they came to Hajar and said: "If you wish, we will be with you, keep you company, and the water is yours." She gave them permission, and they settled with her, and they remained there until Isma'il grew up. Then Hajar died, and Isma'il married a woman from Jurhum. Abraham asked Sarah's permission to visit Hajar, and she gave him permission, but stipulated that he should not stay there. [Tarikh al-Tabari 1/179–180, and he mentioned the rest of the story]. He also mentioned the hadith about the description of the Station of Abraham, and this story has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

﴿Our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾. ﴿So make hearts of people incline towards them﴾, meaning they are frightened, and it is said they yearn towards them. This is a supplication from him (peace be upon him) that God provide them with pilgrimage to His Sacred House.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "If it had said 'the hearts of people will incline towards them,' Jews, Christians and Magians would have made the pilgrimage. But He said ﴿hearts from among the people﴾, among whom are the Muslims."

Mujahid said: "If it had said 'the hearts of people,' Persians, Romans, Turks and Indians would have crowded around it. But He said ﴿hearts from among the people﴾ ... ﴿and provide them with fruits﴾, as You provided the inhabitants of villages with water, ﴿so that they may be grateful﴾. ﴿Our Lord, You indeed know what we conceal and what we disclose﴾ of all our affairs.

Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: "From the grief (al-wajd) is Isma'il and his mother, when He settled her ﴿in an uncultivated valley﴾ ... ﴿nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven﴾."

Some of them said: "This is a connecting statement, about the offspring of Abraham (peace be upon him)."

Others said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿nothing is hidden from God﴾, and this is the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Praise be to God, who has granted me, despite old age, Isma'il and Isaac; indeed my Lord hears supplication﴾."

Ibn Abbas said: "Isma'il was born to Abraham when he was ninety-nine years old, and Isaac was born to him when he was one hundred and twelve years old."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Abraham was given glad tidings of Isaac after one hundred and twelve years."

﴿My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and from my offspring too﴾, and also make them establishers of prayer. ﴿Our Lord, and accept my supplication﴾.

The exegetes said: "That is, my worship." Its parallel is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Supplication is the essence of worship" [Kanz al-Ummal 2/62, no. 3114]. Then he recited: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me﴾ [Qur'an 40:60], so He called supplication worship.

﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾, if they believed and repented. God has informed about the excuse of His Friend for asking forgiveness for his father in Surah al-Tawbah.

﴿And the believers﴾, all of them.

Ibn Abbas said: "From the community of Muhammad." ﴿On the Day the Reckoning takes place﴾, meaning, on the day it appears and becomes manifest. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "He intends: the day the people stand for the reckoning, and mentioning the reckoning is enough without mentioning the people, since it is understood."

It is said: "jannabtuhu, ajnubuhu, janban," and "ajnabtuhu, ijnaban," with the same meaning, and "ajnabuka" and "jannabtuhu, tajniban."

The poet said, and he is Umayyah ibn al-Ashkar al-Laythi:

*"She shakes his cradle out of compassion for him,
and keeps him away, so he does not endure hardships."*

"Idols" (al-asnam) is the plural of "sanam," which is a sculpted image. The poet said:

*"A slender woman, like a palm-branch, shows her inner beauty,
she laughs, revealing sweet, clear-white teeth."*

Ibrahim al-Taymi said in his stories: "Who can feel safe from trial after Abraham, the Friend of God (peace be upon him), when he says: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols. My Lord, they have led many people astray﴾" meaning that many people went astray through them, to the point that they worshipped them. This is from the inverted usage (al-maghlub). Its parallel is His saying: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens his allies﴾, meaning he frightens you with his allies.

﴿Whoever follows me is indeed of me﴾, upon my religion and my creed, ﴿and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Al-Suddi said: its meaning is ﴿and whoever disobeys me﴾, so that he repents.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿and whoever disobeys me﴾ refers to anything short of association (shirk).

Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited the words of Abraham (peace be upon him): ﴿Whoever follows me is indeed of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

And the words of Jesus (peace be upon him): ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants﴾ [Qur'an 5:118], the verse, and he raised his hands and said: "O God, my community! O God, my community!" and wept. God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what is wrong with him." So Gabriel came and asked him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told him what he had said. God said: "O Gabriel, go to Muhammad and say: 'We shall indeed please you regarding your community, and will not grieve you.'"

﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring﴾. What is inserted here, "min" (some of), is for partition, and the meaning of the verse is: I have settled some of my offspring, a son, ﴿in an uncultivated valley﴾, which is Mecca, ﴿near Your Sacred House﴾.

Qatadah said: "The Sacred House is sacred because God has made it inviolable, and disrespecting its right is forbidden." If it is asked, what is the meaning of Abraham's words "near Your House," when Abraham built the House only a long time afterward? It is said the meaning is "near Your Sacred House," which existed before He raised it from the earth, until it was raised in the days of the Flood.

It is also said: "near Your Sacred House" means the House that had already been decreed in Your knowledge, that it would come to be in this land.

The story of the verse, as related by Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, is that Ibn Abbas said: "The first to run between al-Safa and al-Marwah was Hajar, the mother of Isma'il. And the first thing that was introduced was the dragging of garments, for Hajar did that, because when she fled from Sarah she let down her garment so her footprints would be hidden. Abraham brought her and her son Isma'il until he brought them to the place of the House, and he set them down and turned back. She said: 'To whom are you leaving us?' He did not answer her at all. So she said: 'Did God command you to do this?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Then He will not let us be lost.' He said: With the woman was a waterskin containing water, and the water ran out, so she became thirsty, and her milk dried up, and the child became thirsty. She looked at the mountains nearest to the ground, and climbed al-Safa, and listened carefully to see whether she could hear a voice or see anyone, but she heard nothing. So she came down, and when she reached the valley she ran, like a person exhausted who runs without intending to run. Then she looked for the nearest mountain to the ground, climbed al-Marwah, listened carefully to hear a voice or see someone. She heard a voice and said, like a person whose hearing deceives him: "Be quiet," until she was certain. Then she said: "You have made me hear your voice, so help me, for I am lost and whoever is with me is lost." Then there was the angel, who came with her until he brought her to the place of Zamzam, struck the ground with his foot, and a spring gushed forth. The woman hurried and began to pour it into her waterskin.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "May God have mercy on the mother of Isma'il. If she had not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring." The angel said to her: "Do not fear thirst for the people of this land, for this is a spring for the drink of God's guests," and he said: "The father of this boy will come, and they will build a House for God, this is its place."

He said: A caravan from Jurhum passed by, heading for Syria. They saw birds over the mountain, and said: "These birds are circling over water." They came up and saw the woman, so they came to Hajar and said: "If you wish, we will be with you, keep you company, and the water is yours." She gave them permission, and they settled with her, and they remained there until Isma'il grew up. Then Hajar died, and Isma'il married a woman from Jurhum. He also mentioned the hadith about the description of the Station of Abraham, and this story has already passed in Surah Al 'Imran.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 42–52:

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.﴾ Maymun ibn Mihran said: This is a threat to the wrongdoer and a consolation to the wronged [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/310]. ﴿He only defers them﴾, that is, He gives them respite and postpones their punishment.

The majority of readers recited it with the *ta'* (تحسبن, "you think"), and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this, because of the words ﴿And do not think that Allah﴾. Al-Hasan and al-Sulami recited it with the *nun* (نحسبن, "We think").

﴿A Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾: that is, they will not blink, because of the terror of what they see on that Day. This was said by al-Farra'.

﴿Hastening (muhti'in)﴾: Qatadah said: hurrying. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on his authority, said: hurrying onward.

'Abid ibn al-Awza'i and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: *al-ihta'* (الإهطاع) is a flowing run like the run of a wolf.

Mujahid said: gazing continuously.

al-Dahhak said: an intense gaze without blinking, and this is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Kalbi said: looking. Muqatil said: coming forward toward the Fire.

Ibn Zayd said: *al-muhti'* is the one who does not raise his head. The root meaning of *al-ihta'* in the speech of the Arabs is hastening and speeding. It is said: *ahta'a al-ba'iru* in his walk, and *istah-ta'a* when he sped up.

A poet said:

"And one hastening, loose, as if his halter
Were on the top of a trunk of a trimmed acacia."

Another said:

"Hastening in a gentle pace, as if his two cords
Were on a bank of a tall, bulging hill."

Another said:

"Namr ibn Sa'd has ordered me, and I see
That Namr ibn Sa'd is obedient and hastening to me."

﴿Heads raised (muqni'i ru'usihim)﴾: raising them.

al-Qutabi said: *al-muqni'* is the one who raises his head and directs his gaze at what is before him. From this comes *al-iqna'* in prayer.

al-Hasan said: the faces of people on the Day of Resurrection will be toward the sky, no one looking at anyone. The root meaning of *al-iqna'* in the speech of the Arabs is raising the head.

al-Shammakh said:

"They come in the morning to the thorny trees with raised [heads],
Their fangs like the broken ... of the gazelle."

That is, with heads raised toward them so as to reach them.

The reciter said:

"He raised his head toward me and lifted it high,
As if he had seen something that made him greedy."

﴿Their gaze will not return to them﴾: their eyes will not come back to them, from the intensity of the gaze, so they are fixed. ﴿And their hearts are empty (hawa')﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: empty of all good.

Mujahid, Murrah ibn Sharahil and Ibn Zayd said: broken and ruined, with no good and no intellect in them, like your saying of a house in which there is nothing: "It is only air." This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas [Lisan al-'Arab: 9/35].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they will be churning in their bellies, with no place to settle.

Qatadah said: they will be torn out until they are in their throats, not coming out of their mouths and not returning to their places.

al-Akhfash said: hollow, without minds.

The Arabs call every hollow thing *nukhb* and *hawa'*, and from it comes *ahwa'*, which is the space between the earth and the sky.

Zuhayr said, describing his she-camel:

"The rider on her was like a ... of the ostriches, whose breast is air."

Hassan said:

"Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me:
You are a hollow, empty, air."

﴿And warn the people of the Day when the punishment comes to them﴾: and it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then those who did wrong will say﴾: this is a conjunction with "the Day when it comes to them", and it is not the answer, which is why it is in this form. Those who did wrong are those who associated partners [with Allah]. ﴿Our Lord, delay us﴾: give us respite ﴿for a short term﴾, and this is the worldly life; that is, return us to it. ﴿We will answer Your call and follow the Messengers﴾, so they will be answered. ﴿Did you not swear before﴾ in the abode of the world ﴿that there would be no passing away for you?﴾ That is, that you would not be resurrected. This is His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that Allah would not raise up one who dies﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 38]. ...

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ in the world, through disbelief and disobedience: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and others. ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth parables for you.﴾ ﴿And they had planned their plot, but their plot was with Allah﴾, that is, the recompense for their plot. ﴿Though their plot was [such that]...﴾

The majority recited it with the *nun* (كان مكرهم).

'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy recited: ﴿and though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾ with the addition of *ma yazal* (ما يزال).

﴿That the mountains would be moved by it﴾: the majority recited the first *lam* (لتزول) with a *kasra* and the second with a *fatha*.

Ibn Jurayj and al-Kisa'i recited with a *fatha* on the first *mim* and a *damma* on the second (مكرُهم), in agreement with the reading of the majority. al-Zajjaj said regarding His saying ﴿And though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾, that is, their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it.

It is the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the command of Islam and its firmness, like the firmness of the lofty mountains, because Allah promised him to make His religion prevail over all religions. It was also said that its meaning is: "Their plot was [such that]..."

al-Hasan said: "[Their plot was] too weak and feeble for the mountains to be moved by it." He said: there are five places in the Qur'an where *in* (إن) means *ma* (ما): His saying ﴿And though their plot was...﴾, and His saying ﴿Had We intended to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to do [it]﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 17], and His saying ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 81], ﴿in that wherein We have established you﴾ [Surah al-Ahqaf: 26], and His saying ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 94]. As for the one who recited the first *lam* with a *fatha*, it is on account of the greatness of their plot [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/380].

Ibn Jarir said: The preferred reading is the first, because if it were the second, it would not be established; and it would be: "Their plot was [such that]..."

What 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and others mentioned: They said: Nimrod the tyrant, who argued with Abraham about his Lord, said: "If what Abraham says is true, I will not stop until I know what is in the sky." So he took four young vultures, fed them meat and raised them until they grew strong and robust. Then he sat in a chest (tabut) and placed another man with him. He made for it a door at the top and a door at the bottom, tied the chest to the legs of the vultures, and hung the meat above the chest on a stick. Then he released the vultures, and they flew up, desiring the meat, until they went far into the air [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/320, with variation].

"And one hastening, loose, as if his halter
Were on the top of a trunk of a trimmed acacia."

Another said:

"Hastening in a gentle pace, as if his two cords

Another said:

The Arabs call every hollow thing *nukhb* and *hawa'*, and from it comes *ahwa'*, which is the space between the earth and the sky.

Zuhayr said, describing his she-camel:

"The rider on her was like a ... of the ostriches, whose breast is air."

Hassan said:

"Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me:
You are a hollow, empty, air."

﴿And warn the people of the Day when the punishment comes to them﴾: and it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then those who did wrong will say﴾: this is a conjunction with "the Day when it comes to them", and it is not the answer, which is why it is in this form. The majority recited it with the *nun* (كان مكرهم).

Mujahid said: gazing continuously.

al-Dahhak said: an intense gaze without blinking, and this is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Kalbi said: looking. Muqatil said: coming forward toward the Fire.

Ibn Zayd said: *al-muhti'* is the one who does not raise his head. The root meaning of *al-ihta'* in the speech of the Arabs is hastening and speeding. It is said: *ahta'a al-ba'iru* in his walk, and *istah-ta'a* when he sped up.

A poet said:

"And one hastening, loose, as if his halter
Were on the top of a trunk of a trimmed acacia."

Another said:

"Hastening in a gentle pace, as if his two cords
Were on a bank of a tall, bulging hill."

Another said:

"Namr ibn Sa'd has ordered me, and I see
That Namr ibn Sa'd is obedient and hastening to me."

"They come in the morning to the thorny trees with raised [heads],
Their fangs like the broken ... of the gazelle."

That is, with heads raised toward them so as to reach them.

The reciter said:

"He raised his head toward me and lifted it high,
As if he had seen something that made him greedy."

On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will become fire, and Paradise will be behind it, its maidens and its cups visible, and people will be bridled with sweat, and they will not yet have reached the reckoning."

Ka'b said: "The heavens will become gardens, and the place of the sea will become fire, and the earth will be changed to another [earth]."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The earth is that same earth, but it will be entirely changed, along with its mountains and rivers." Then he recited:

"People are not the people I knew,
Nor is the abode the abode I used to know."

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/254]

In confirmation of Ibn 'Abbas's statement, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The earth will be changed into other than the earth, and He will spread it out and extend it like a tanned hide of 'Ukaz, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation. Then Allah will drive the creation with one driving, and they will be in the second [earth] in the same places as they were in the first. Whoever was in its belly will be in its belly, and whoever was upon its back will be upon its back" [170] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/383].

It was also said: "The earth will be changed into other than the earth" means into an earth [white like silver].

He said: "They will be the guests of Allah, and what is with Him will not fail them."

﴿And they will come forth (wa baraza)﴾: they will appear and come out of their graves ﴿before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾: the Overpowering, who does what He wills and subdues the servants with death. ﴿And you will see the criminals (al-mujrimin)﴾: the polytheists ﴿that Day bound together in chains﴾: tied to one another. It was also said: bound together with the devils. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 22], and they are the devils. Ibn Zayd said: their hands and their feet are bound to their necks in fetters and shackles. Its singular is *saf'd* (صفد), and *al-sifad* is also a fetter, and its plural is *sifd*. It is said: "I shackled him with shackles (safadan) and fetters (asfadan)," meaning to multiply [the fetters]. I say: "I shackled him with intensive shackling (tasfid)."

'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"So they brought the plunder and the captives,
And the sons of kings, shackled, as prisoners."

﴿Their garments (sarabilahum)﴾: their shirts. Its singular is *sirbal*, and the verb from it is *tasarbala* and *sarbala ghayrī*. ﴿Of tar (qatiran)﴾: which is what camels are coated with for scabies, and it is called *al-khadkhad* [see al-Sihah: 3/74].

"Dark-colored, as if the sweat of ... had been put on him,
Tar and coarse wool had clothed him."

Allah says: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper (qitran)﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 96]. *Al-aan* is that whose heat has reached its end. Allah says: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding (hamim aan) water﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 44]. ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces﴾ until His saying: ﴿This [Qur'an] is a message (balagh)﴾: a conveyance and admonition ﴿for the people, that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 14, verses 42–52:

﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.﴾ Maymun ibn Mihran said: This is a threat to the wrongdoer and a consolation to the wronged [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/310]. ﴿He only defers them﴾, that is, He gives them respite and postpones their punishment.

The majority of readers recited it with the *ta'* (تحسبن, "you think"), and Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this, because of the words ﴿And do not think that Allah﴾. Al-Hasan and al-Sulami recited it with the *nun* (نحسبن, "We think").

﴿A Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾: that is, they will not blink, because of the terror of what they see on that Day. This was said by al-Farra'.

﴿Hastening (muhti'in)﴾: Qatadah said: hurrying. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on his authority, said: hurrying onward.

'Abid ibn al-Awza'i and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: *al-ihta'* (الإهطاع) is a flowing run like the run of a wolf.

Mujahid said: gazing continuously.

al-Dahhak said: an intense gaze without blinking, and this is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Kalbi said: looking. Muqatil said: coming forward toward the Fire.

Ibn Zayd said: *al-muhti'* is the one who does not raise his head. The root meaning of *al-ihta'* in the speech of the Arabs is hastening and speeding. It is said: *ahta'a al-ba'iru* in his walk, and *istah-ta'a* when he sped up.

A poet said:

"And one hastening, loose, as if his halter
Were on the top of a trunk of a trimmed acacia."

Another said:

"Hastening in a gentle pace, as if his two cords
Were on a bank of a tall, bulging hill."

Another said:

"Namr ibn Sa'd has ordered me, and I see
That Namr ibn Sa'd is obedient and hastening to me."

﴿Heads raised (muqni'i ru'usihim)﴾: raising them.

al-Qutabi said: *al-muqni'* is the one who raises his head and directs his gaze at what is before him. From this comes *al-iqna'* in prayer.

al-Hasan said: the faces of people on the Day of Resurrection will be toward the sky, no one looking at anyone. The root meaning of *al-iqna'* in the speech of the Arabs is raising the head.

al-Shammakh said:

"They come in the morning to the thorny trees with raised [heads],
Their fangs like the broken ... of the gazelle."

That is, with heads raised toward them so as to reach them.

The reciter said:

"He raised his head toward me and lifted it high,
As if he had seen something that made him greedy."

﴿Their gaze will not return to them﴾: their eyes will not come back to them, from the intensity of the gaze, so they are fixed. ﴿And their hearts are empty (hawa')﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: empty of all good.

Mujahid, Murrah ibn Sharahil and Ibn Zayd said: broken and ruined, with no good and no intellect in them, like your saying of a house in which there is nothing: "It is only air." This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas [Lisan al-'Arab: 9/35].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they will be churning in their bellies, with no place to settle.

Qatadah said: they will be torn out until they are in their throats, not coming out of their mouths and not returning to their places.

al-Akhfash said: hollow, without minds.

The Arabs call every hollow thing *nukhb* and *hawa'*, and from it comes *ahwa'*, which is the space between the earth and the sky.

Zuhayr said, describing his she-camel:

"The rider on her was like a ... of the ostriches, whose breast is air."

Hassan said:

"Let me convey to Abu Sufyan from me:
You are a hollow, empty, air."

﴿And warn the people of the Day when the punishment comes to them﴾: and it is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then those who did wrong will say﴾: this is a conjunction with "the Day when it comes to them", and it is not the answer, which is why it is in this form. Those who did wrong are those who associated partners [with Allah]. ﴿Our Lord, delay us﴾: give us respite ﴿for a short term﴾, and this is the worldly life; that is, return us to it. ﴿We will answer Your call and follow the Messengers﴾, so they will be answered. ﴿Did you not swear before﴾ in the abode of the world ﴿that there would be no passing away for you?﴾ That is, that you would not be resurrected. This is His saying: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their strongest oaths that Allah would not raise up one who dies﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 38]. ...

﴿And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves﴾ in the world, through disbelief and disobedience: the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and others. ﴿And it became clear to you how We dealt with them, and We set forth parables for you.﴾ ﴿And they had planned their plot, but their plot was with Allah﴾, that is, the recompense for their plot. ﴿Though their plot was [such that]...﴾

The majority recited it with the *nun* (كان مكرهم).

'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy recited: ﴿and though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾ with the addition of *ma yazal* (ما يزال).

﴿That the mountains would be moved by it﴾: the majority recited the first *lam* (لتزول) with a *kasra* and the second with a *fatha*.

Ibn Jurayj and al-Kisa'i recited with a *fatha* on the first *mim* and a *damma* on the second (مكرُهم), in agreement with the reading of the majority. al-Zajjaj said regarding His saying ﴿And though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾, that is, their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it.

It is the command of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the command of Islam and its firmness, like the firmness of the lofty mountains, because Allah promised him to make His religion prevail over all religions. It was also said that its meaning is: "Their plot was [such that]..."

al-Hasan said: "[Their plot was] too weak and feeble for the mountains to be moved by it." He said: there are five places in the Qur'an where *in* (إن) means *ma* (ما): His saying ﴿And though their plot was...﴾, and His saying ﴿Had We intended to take a pastime, We would have taken it from Ourselves, if We were to do [it]﴾ [Surah al-Anbiya': 17], and His saying ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [Surah al-Zukhruf: 81], ﴿in that wherein We have established you﴾ [Surah al-Ahqaf: 26], and His saying ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 94]. As for the one who recited the first *lam* with a *fatha*, it is on account of the greatness of their plot [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 9/380].

Ibn Jarir said: The preferred reading is the first, because if it were the second, it would not be established; and it would be: "Their plot was [such that]..."

What 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) and others mentioned: They said: Nimrod the tyrant, who argued with Abraham about his Lord, said: "If what Abraham says is true, I will not stop until I know what is in the sky." So he took four young vultures, fed them meat and raised them until they grew strong and robust. Then he sat in a chest (tabut) and placed another man with him. He made for it a door at the top and a door at the bottom, tied the chest to the legs of the vultures, and hung the meat above the chest on a stick. Then he released the vultures, and they flew up, desiring the meat, until they went far into the air [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/320, with variation].

Nimrod said to his companion: "Open the first door and look at the sky; do you see anything of it?" He opened it and looked, and said: "The sky is as it was." Then he said: "Open the lower door and look at the earth; how do you see it?" He did so and said: "I see the earth like a white sea, and the mountains like smoke." The vultures flew higher until they came between them and the chest. Then he said to his companion: "Open both doors." He opened the upper one, and behold, the sky was as it was; and he opened the lower one, and behold, the earth was black and dark. Then it was called out: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?"

'Ikrimah said: There was with him in the chest a boy who carried a bow and arrows, and he shot at them, and the arrow came back to him smeared with blood. He said: "You have been sufficient for yourself, O God of the sky." They differed about what the arrow was smeared with.

'Ikrimah said: a fish that ransomed itself to Allah from a sea in the air, suspended.

Some of them said: from a bird of the birds that the arrow struck.

They said: Then Nimrod ordered his companion to strike the stick and lower the meat, and he did so. The vultures descended with the chest, and the mountains heard the rustling of the chest among the vultures, and they were terrified, and thought that something had happened in the sky, or that the Resurrection had come. That is His saying: ﴿And though their plot was [such that] the mountains would be moved by it﴾.

﴿So do not think that Allah is breaking His promise to His Messengers﴾, by giving victory to His allies and destruction to His enemies. In the statement there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "And let not Allah be thought to break His promise to His Messengers", because breaking [a promise] occurs with the promise.

A poet says:

"You see the bull in it entering the shade with its head,
And the rest of it exposed to the sun, entirely."

al-Qutabi said: it is from the front [part] that the back [part] clarifies, and the back [part] that the front clarifies. It is your saying: "He breaks His promise to His Messengers" and "He breaks His Messengers' promise", because breaking occurs with the promise as it occurs with the Messengers.

Were on the top of a trunk of a trimmed acacia."

As if he had seen something that made him greedy."

Hassan said:

It was also said: bound together with the devils. Its explanation is His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong, and their spouses, and what they used to worship﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 22], and they are the devils. Ibn Zayd said: their hands and their feet are bound to their necks in fetters and shackles. Its singular is *saf'd* (صفد), and *al-sifad* is also a fetter, and its plural is *sifd*. It is said: "I shackled him with shackles (safadan) and fetters (asfadan)," meaning to multiply [the fetters]. I say: "I shackled him with intensive shackling (tasfid)."

'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

"So they brought the plunder and the captives,
And the sons of kings, shackled, as prisoners."

﴿Their garments (sarabilahum)﴾: their shirts. Its singular is *sirbal*, and the verb from it is *tasarbala* and *sarbala ghayrī*. ﴿Of tar (qatiran)﴾: which is what camels are coated with for scabies, and it is called *al-khadkhad* [see al-Sihah: 3/74].

al-Hasan said, and 'Isa ibn 'Umar recited: *qatran* with a *fatha* on the *qaf* and a sukun on the *ta'*. There is a third dialect: *qitran* with a *kasra* on the *qaf* and a sukun on the *ta'*. From it is the saying of Abu al-Najm:

"Dark-colored, as if the sweat of ... had been put on him,
Tar and coarse wool had clothed him."

'Ikrimah recited, according to the transmission of Zayd: *qatrin aan* (قَطْرٍ آنٍ), as two tanwin-ed words, *qatrin* and *aanin*. *Al-qatr* is molten yellow copper. Allah says: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper (qitran)﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 96]. *Al-aan* is that whose heat has reached its end. Allah says: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding (hamim aan) water﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 44]. ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces﴾ until His saying: ﴿This [Qur'an] is a message (balagh)﴾: a conveyance and admonition ﴿for the people, that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed.﴾
